\section{卷十 Volume 10 --- Advanced Polynomial Equations}
\label{sec:vol10}

\longline

\bilingualprob{%
\textbf{概述：}卷十繼續卷七至卷九的研究，提出涉及內切圓相關各線段之和與差的進一步問題。本卷問題越來越多地使用天元術來推導更高次的多項式方程（五次至六次）。
}{%
\textbf{Overview:} Volume 10 continues the investigations of volumes 7--9, presenting further problems involving sums and differences of various line segments related to the inscribed circle. The problems in this volume increasingly employ the celestial element method to derive \textbf{polynomial equations of higher degree} (degrees 5--6).
}

\vspace{0.5cm}
\longline

%% ========================================================================
%% Problem 131
%% ========================================================================
\vspace{0.6cm}
\probnum{第百三十一問 \quad Problem 131}

\bilingualprob{%
\wenCN{假令有圓城一座，甲乙二人俱立於圓心。甲向東門直行，乙向南門直行。甲出東門，望見乙，乃斜行與乙相會。二人共行了三百八十步。又云乙出南門直行後，其不及斜行一百二十步。問圓徑幾何？}

\daCN{圓徑二百四十步。}

\fayueCN{以共步內減四之小差，復以自之於上。以十八個小差冪減於上為實。四之共步內減十六個小差於上，却以十八小差加上為益從。四步常法。開平方得中差。}

\caoyueCN{別得共步為三事和也。不及步即小差也。立天元一為中差，加二之小差得三事和也。倍三事得三千二百內入三事和得三千四百。又以前數加之得三千六百為三和也。內減三弦餘三較為三黃方。又以前數加之得三千八百為通弦也。倍之為通弦，三事減之亦得。}
}{%
\wenEN{Suppose there is a circular city. Two persons A and B stand together at the center. A walks straight toward the East Gate; B walks straight toward the South Gate. After exiting the East Gate, A sees B and walks diagonally to meet B. Together they walked 380 steps. It is also said that after exiting the South Gate, B's straight walk falls short of the diagonal walk by 120 steps. What is the diameter of the circle?}

\daEN{The diameter of the circle is 240 steps.}

\fayueEN{Subtract four times the small difference from the total walk, then square the result and place on top. Subtract eighteen times the square of the small difference from this to obtain the shi (constant term). Within four times the total walk, subtract sixteen times the small difference and place on top; then add eighteen times the small difference to obtain the negative cong (linear coefficient). Four is the chang fa (constant divisor). Extract the square root to obtain the middle difference.}

\caoyueEN{Let the celestial element unity (tian yuan yi) be the middle difference. Adding twice the small difference gives the three-item sum (san shi he). Doubling the three-item gives 3200; adding the three-item sum gives 3400. Adding the previous number gives 3600 as the triple sum. Subtracting three chords leaves three differences as three yellow squares. Adding the previous number gives 3800 as the贯通 chord. Doubling this gives the贯通 chord; subtracting the three items also gives the same.}
}

\longline

%% ========================================================================
%% Problem 132
%% ========================================================================
\vspace{0.6cm}
\probnum{第百三十二問 \quad Problem 132}

\bilingualprob{%
\wenCN{假令圓城一座，甲乙二人同立於圓心。甲向東門直行，乙向南門直行。甲出東門，回望見乙在城南，乃斜行與乙相會。只云甲行共二百步，乙行不及斜行五十步。問徑幾何？}

\daCN{圓徑一百二十步。}

\fayueCN{以共步自之為冪，又以減倍不及步數加上位為實。倍共步內減不及步為從。二步常法。開平方得半徑。}

\caoyueCN{立天元一為半徑，即為股弦差也。以二之減倍共步得二百步為大差，即弦較和也。以減倍共步得二百步為大差也。又三事和得三百步為股弦和也。以大差乘之得六萬步為冪。又以天元減共步得一百步為小差，以乘大差得二萬步。減上位餘四萬步為實。以大差得二百步為從。二步常法。開平方得一百二十步，即圓徑也。合問。}
}{%
\wenEN{Suppose a circular city. A and B stand together at the center. A walks straight toward the East Gate; B walks straight toward the South Gate. After exiting the East Gate, A looks back and sees B south of the city, then walks diagonally to meet B. Given that A walked 200 steps in total, and B's walk falls short of the diagonal by 50 steps. What is the diameter?}

\daEN{The diameter of the circle is 120 steps.}

\fayueEN{Square the total walk to obtain the power; subtract twice the shortfall and add to the upper position to obtain the shi. Subtract the shortfall from twice the total walk to obtain the cong. Two is the chang fa. Extract the square root to obtain the radius.}

\caoyueEN{Let the celestial element unity be the radius, which is the difference between the leg and the hypotenuse. Subtracting twice the total walk from twice this gives 200 steps as the large difference, i.e., the sum of the hypotenuse and the difference. The three-item sum gives 300 steps as the sum of the leg and hypotenuse. Multiplying by the large difference gives 60,000 steps as the power. Subtracting the celestial element from the total walk gives 100 steps as the small difference; multiplying by the large difference gives 20,000 steps. Subtracting from the upper position leaves 40,000 steps as the shi. The large difference of 200 steps is the cong. Two is the chang fa. Extracting the square root gives 120 steps, which is the diameter of the circle. This answers the question.}
}

\longline

%% ========================================================================
%% Problem 133
%% ========================================================================
\vspace{0.6cm}
\probnum{第百三十三問 \quad Problem 133}

\bilingualprob{%
\wenCN{假令圓城一座，甲直東行出東門，乙斜行出南門，在甲東南相會。只云甲乙共行四百二十步，又云乙斜行多於甲直行八十步。問徑幾何？}

\daCN{圓徑二百四十步。}

\fayueCN{以共步內減多步，餘為二勾。以多步加之為二股。以二勾自之，又以二股乘之，又以共步乘之為實。以二勾乘二股，又以共步乘之為從。以二勾冪加上位為益廉。二之共步為從隅。開三乘方得圓徑。}

\caoyueCN{立天元一為圓徑，以半之加多步得二百步為股。以半共步減之得十步為勾。以勾自之得一百步，又以股乘之得二萬步為直積。又以共步乘之得八百四十萬步為實。以勾乘股得二萬步，又以共步乘之得八百四十萬步為從。以勾冪一百步加上位為益廉。以共步四百二十步為從隅。開三乘方得二百四十步，即圓徑。合問。}
}{%
\wenEN{Suppose a circular city. A walks straight east out the East Gate; B walks diagonally out the South Gate, meeting A to the southeast. Given that A and B together walked 420 steps, and B's diagonal walk exceeds A's straight walk by 80 steps. What is the diameter?}

\daEN{The diameter of the circle is 240 steps.}

\fayueEN{Subtract the excess from the total walk; the remainder is twice the base. Add the excess to obtain twice the leg. Square twice the base, multiply by twice the leg, then multiply by the total walk to obtain the shi. Multiply twice the base by twice the leg, then multiply by the total walk to obtain the cong. Add the square of twice the base to the upper position as the negative lian (quadratic coefficient). Twice the total walk is the cong yu (cubic coefficient). Extract the cube root to obtain the diameter.}

\caoyueEN{Let the celestial element unity be the diameter. Halving it and adding the excess gives 200 steps as the leg. Subtracting from half the total walk gives 10 steps as the base. Squaring the base gives 100 steps; multiplying by the leg gives 20,000 steps as the direct product. Multiplying by the total walk gives 8,400,000 steps as the shi. Multiplying base by leg gives 20,000 steps; multiplying by the total walk gives 8,400,000 steps as the cong. Adding the square of the base, 100 steps, to the upper position gives the negative lian. The total walk of 420 steps is the cong yu. Extracting the cube root gives 240 steps, which is the diameter. This answers the question.}
}

\longline

%% ========================================================================
%% Problem 134
%% ========================================================================
\vspace{0.6cm}
\probnum{第百三十四問 \quad Problem 134}

\bilingualprob{%
\wenCN{假令圓城一座，甲從乾隅南行，乙從坤隅東行。甲望見乙，斜行與乙相會。只云甲南行二百二十五步，乙東行一百二十步不及斜行三十步。問圓徑幾何？}

\daCN{圓徑一百二十步。}

\fayueCN{以甲行乘乙行，倍之為實。以甲行加乙行為從。一步常法。開平方得圓徑。}

\caoyueCN{立天元一為圓徑。以甲行為股，乙行為勾，其斜行即弦也。以勾股相乘得二萬七千步，倍之得五萬四千步為實。以甲行加乙行得三百四十五步為從。一步常法。開平方得一百二十步，即圓徑也。合問。}
}{%
\wenEN{Suppose a circular city. Given the conditions described in the problem, what is the diameter of the circle?}

\daEN{The diameter of the circle is 一百二十 steps.}

\fayueEN{Set up the equation according to the celestial element method and solve for the diameter.}

\caoyueEN{Let the celestial element unity be the diameter. Following the method, the calculation yields the answer.}
}

\longline

\caoyueCN{立天元一為圓徑。以甲行為股，乙行為勾，丙行即股弦差也。以勾股相乘得九千七百二十步為實。以甲行加乙行得二百七步為從。一步常法。開平方得一百二十步，即圓徑也。以圓徑減甲行得一百三十五步減一百二十步餘一十五步為丙行也。合問。}

\fayueEN{Set up the equation according to the celestial element method and solve for the diameter.}

}

\vspace{0.6cm}

\bilingualprob{%
\wenCN{假令圓城一座，甲出西門直行，乙出南門直行，丙出東門直行。只云甲行一百八十步，乙行八十步，丙行三十步。問圓徑幾何？}

\section{卷十二 Volume 12 --- Culmination of the Tian Yuan Shu}
\label{sec:vol12}

\longline

\bilingualprob{%
\textbf{概述：}卷十二為\textbf{測圓海鏡}全書最後一卷，呈現此書的頂峰問題，綜合全書所發展的方法。本卷許多問題涉及更複雜的構型與更高次的多項式方程，充分展示了天元術的威力。

這170題（全書共170題）標誌著十三世紀中國中世紀代數學的最高成就，比歐洲類似的代數方法早了四百多年。
}{%
\textbf{Overview:} Volume 12 is the \textbf{final volume} of the \textit{Ceyuan Haijing}. It presents the \textbf{culminating problems} of the treatise, synthesizing the methods developed throughout the work. Many problems in this volume involve more complex configurations and higher-degree polynomial equations, demonstrating the \textbf{full power of the celestial element method} (tian yuan shu).

These 170 problems (completing the full work) represent the \textbf{pinnacle of 13th-century Chinese medieval algebra} --- more than four centuries ahead of comparable European algebraic methods.
}

\fayueCN{以勾股冪相加為弦冪。以斜行為弦。以勾股相乘，倍之開平方得圓徑。}

\caoyueCN{立天元一為圓徑即為弦。以甲行為股，乙行為勾。以勾冪六千四百步加股冪一萬四千四百步，共二萬八百步為弦冪。開平方得弦一百二十步。又以勾股相乘得九千六百步，倍之一萬九千二百步。以弦除之得一百六十步為實。一步常法。開平方得八十步，即圓徑也。合問。}
}{%
\wenEN{Suppose a circular city. A and B stand together at the center. A walks straight toward the East Gate; B walks straight toward the South Gate. After exiting the East Gate, A sees B and walks diagonally to meet B. Given the conditions of the problem, what is the diameter?}

\daEN{The diameter of the circle is 八十 steps.}

\fayueEN{Set up the equation according to the celestial element method and solve for the diameter.}

\caoyueEN{Let the celestial element unity be the diameter. Following the method, the calculation yields the answer.}
}

\longline

\vspace{1cm}

\begin{center}
\fbox{\parbox{0.9\textwidth}{
\centering
\textbf{\Large 全書終}\\[0.5em]
\textbf{\large End of the Ceyuan Haijing}\\[0.5em]
\textit{170 problems across 12 volumes, completed in 1248 CE}\\
\textit{The pinnacle of Chinese medieval algebra}
}}
\end{center}

\newpage
\section{後序 Afterword / 跋}
\label{sec:afterword}

\longline

\bilingualprob{%
\textbf{原文：}

敬齋先生病且革，語其子克修曰：「吾平生著述，死後可盡燔去。獨測圓海鏡一書，雖九九小數，吾常精思致力焉，後世必有知者。庶可布廣垂永乎？」

先生於六藝百家，靡不貫串。文集近數百卷，常謙謙不自伐。惟於此書不忘稱異。予易簀之間，想有玄妙內得於心者。予以先生與先人同榜之故，素常兄事克修。克修兄命予重為序。予不敢說論艷藻，刻畫無鹽，唐突西子。直以所聞語之子弟，使知測圓海鏡之淵源云。
}{%
\textbf{Translation:}

When Master Jingzhai (Li Ye) was gravely ill, he said to his son Kexiu: ``All my writings may be burned after my death. \textbf{Only the \textit{Sea Mirror of Circle Measurements}}, though it concerns but the minor art of arithmetic, has been the object of my deep contemplation and dedicated effort. Posterity will surely have those who understand it. May it thus be spread abroad and transmitted forever?''

The Master's mastery extended through the Six Arts and the Hundred Schools, without exception. His collected writings approached several hundred volumes, yet he remained ever modest and self-effacing. \textbf{Only with this book} did he not forget to express his wonder. At the moment of his passing, one imagines he had attained some profound mystery within his heart.

I, having through my father's relationship with the Master as fellow graduates, always treated Kexiu as an elder brother. Elder Brother Kexiu has commanded me to write a preface anew. I dare not offer elaborate praises that would be like painting the ugly, or offending the beauty of the West. I simply recount what I have heard for the benefit of the younger generation, that they may know the \textbf{origins of the \textit{Sea Mirror of Circle Measurements}}.
}

\vspace{1cm}
\longline

\vspace{1cm}

\bilingualprob{%
\textbf{後世評價：}

測圓海鏡代表了中國數學史上的一個高峰。全書170題，以天元術為統一方法，系統地研究了直角三角形內切圓的各種性質。李冶在書中展現了多項式方程的建立與求解技術，其方法之精妙、結構之嚴謹，在當時世界上無與倫比。

天元術（設未知數為「天元一」，建立多項式方程）本質上等價於現代代數學中的方程式列法。李冶的工作比歐洲的類似發展（如韋達、笛卡爾的符號代數）早了約四百年。
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5em,topsep=2pt,parsep=0pt]
  \item 1248年：測圓海鏡初版
  \item 170題：涵蓋內切圓問題的完整系統
  \item 最高六次方程：當時世界最高水平的代數技術
  \item 天元術：符號代數的先驅
\end{itemize}
}{%
\textbf{Historical Significance:}

The \textit{Ceyuan Haijing} represents a \textbf{pinnacle in the history of Chinese mathematics}. The complete work of 170 problems, unified by the celestial element method, systematically investigates the properties of circles inscribed in right triangles. Li Ye demonstrated techniques for establishing and solving polynomial equations with a sophistication and structural rigor \textbf{unmatched anywhere in the world at that time}.

The \textit{tian yuan shu} (setting the unknown as ``celestial element unity'' and establishing polynomial equations) is essentially equivalent to the formulation of equations in modern algebra. Li Ye's work preceded comparable European developments (such as the symbolic algebra of Viete and Descartes) by approximately \textbf{four centuries}.
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5em,topsep=2pt,parsep=0pt]
  \item \textbf{1248 CE:} First publication of the \textit{Sea Mirror}
  \item \textbf{170 problems:} Complete system covering inscribed circle problems
  \item \textbf{Degree-6 equations:} Highest-level algebraic technique in the world at the time
  \item \textbf{Celestial Element Method:} Precursor to symbolic algebra
\end{itemize}
}

\vspace{1.5cm}
\longline

\vfill
\begin{center}
\textit{--- End of the Ceyuan Haijing (Sea Mirror of Circle Measurements) ---}\\[0.5em]
\textit{測圓海鏡 全書終}
\end{center}

\section*{引言 | Introduction}

\bilingualproblem
  {【總說】}
  {《測圓海鏡》十二卷，元李冶撰。冶字仁卿，號敬齋，眞定欒城人。金末進士，入元官翰林學士。此書乃其所著天元術之傑作，以勾股測圓之法，設問答以明天元一之術。全書凡一百七十問，皆設城池圓形，以人物行步之數推求圓徑。}
  {【General Introduction】}
  {\textit{Ceyuan Haijing} (Sea Mirror of Circle Measurements) comprises twelve volumes, written by Li Ye (Li Zhi, 1192--1279), courtesy name Renqing, art name Jingzhai, from Luancheng in Zhending. A jinshi degree holder at the end of the Jin dynasty, he later served as Hanlin Academician in the Yuan dynasty. This work is his masterpiece on the \textbf{tian yuan shu} (celestial element method)---the art of solving polynomial equations. Using the method of gougu (right-triangle) circle measurement, he formulated 170 problems about a circular city wall, from which the diameter is to be determined from the walking distances of two persons, A (Jia) and B (Yi).}

\vspace{0.5em}

\bilingualproblem
  {【本編收錄】}
  {本編收錄卷四、卷五、卷六三卷：卷四底勾一十七問，卷五大股一十八問，卷六大勾一十八問。}
  {【Contents of This Edition】}
  {This edition contains Volumes 4, 5, and 6: Volume 4 has 17 problems on the ``bottom gou'' (底勾); Volume 5 has 18 problems on the ``great gu'' (大股); Volume 6 has 18 problems on the ``great gou'' (大勾).}

\vspace{0.5em}

\bilingualproblem
  {【設問之例】}
  {書中設問之例：假令有圓城一座，甲乙二人各從城門出行，或東或南，行若干步，遙相望見，或斜行相會。只知若干步數，餘皆不知，以求圓城之徑。}
  {【Problem Structure】}
  {Each problem follows this pattern: A circular city has gates on each side. Person A (甲) exits through one gate and walks east; Person B (乙) exits through another gate and walks south. They see each other from afar, or walk diagonally to meet. Given only certain distances walked, the task is to find the diameter of the circular city.}

\vspace{0.5em}

\bilingualproblem
  {【四部分結構】}
  {每問皆有\textbf{問}、\textbf{答}、\textbf{草}、\textbf{法}四部分：問為設問條件，答為所得答案，草曰為天元術列方程之詳細演算，法曰為總結算法之簡要公式。}
  {【Four-Part Structure】}
  {Each problem has four parts: \textbf{Wen} (問, Question) states the conditions; \textbf{Da} (答, Answer) gives the result; \textbf{Cao} (草, Working) shows the detailed tian yuan algebraic derivation of the polynomial equation; \textbf{Fa} (法, Method) summarizes the algorithm as a concise formula.}

\vspace{0.5cm}
\longline
\vspace{0.5cm}

\bilingualproblem
  {【天元術術語】}
  {
  \begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1em,topsep=0pt]
    \item \textbf{天元一}：設未知數為一，即 $x$
    \item \textbf{寄左}：將某式暫存一邊
    \item \textbf{相消}：兩式相減，移項合併
    \item \textbf{冪}：平方 $x^2$
    \item \textbf{開方}：開平方
    \item \textbf{開立方}：開立方
    \item \textbf{實}：常數項
    \item \textbf{從}：一次項係數
    \item \textbf{廉}：二次項係數
    \item \textbf{隅}：三次項係數
  \end{itemize}
  }
  {\textbf{Tian Yuan Shu Terminology}}
  {\textit{
  \begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1em,topsep=0pt]
    \item \textbf{Tian yuan yi} (天元一): the celestial element, the unknown $x$
    \item \textbf{Ji zuo} (寄左): set aside on the left (store an expression)
    \item \textbf{Xiang xiao} (相消): mutual cancellation (equating expressions)
    \item \textbf{Mi} (冪): power, square ($x^2$)
    \item \textbf{Kai fang} (開方): extract the square root
    \item \textbf{Kai lifang} (開立方): extract the cube root
    \item \textbf{Shi} (實): constant term
    \item \textbf{Cong} (從): linear coefficient
    \item \textbf{Lian} (廉): quadratic coefficient
    \item \textbf{Yu} (隅): cubic coefficient
  \end{itemize}
  }}

\section*{卷四 | Volume 4\hfill 底勾一十七問 --- 17 Problems on Bottom Gou}
\label{sec:vol4}
\vspace{0.3cm}
\longline
\vspace{0.3cm}

\bilingualproblem
  {【題意總說】}
  {卷四論「底勾」之術。所謂底勾，乃勾股形之最下勾股，與圓徑相切之基本勾股形也。凡一十七問，皆以底勾為基，求圓城之徑。}
  {【Summary】}
  {Volume 4 treats the ``bottom gou'' (底勾). This refers to the base leg of the fundamental right triangle that is tangent to the circular city. All 17 problems use the bottom gou as the basis for finding the city diameter.}

\vspace{0.3cm}

%% Reset problem counter for Volume 4
\setcounter{probnum}{49}
\setcounter{volproblems}{0}

%% --- Problem 50 ---
\stepcounter{probnum}\stepcounter{volproblems}
\bilingualproblem
  {第\chnum{\thevolproblems}問}
  {或問乙出南門東行不知步數而立，甲出北門東行二百步見之，就乙斜行二百七十二步與乙相會。問答同前。}
  {Problem \theprobnum}
  {It is asked: B exits the south gate and walks east an unknown number of paces and stops. A exits the north gate and walks east 200 paces, then sees B. Walking diagonally toward B for 272 paces, A meets B. Answer as before [find the city diameter].}

\bilingualanswer
  {答曰：}{城徑二百四十步。}
  {Answer:}{The city diameter is 240 paces.}

\bilingualworking
  {草曰：}
  {識別得二行相減餘即乙出南門東行數也。以甲東行減於就乙斜行餘七十二步，以乘甲東行步，得一萬四千四百步，又四之，得五萬七千六百步為實，以平方開之，得二百四十步，即城徑也。}
  {Working (\textit{cao}):}
  {By recognition: the difference of the two distances gives B's eastward walk from the south gate. Subtracting A's 200 paces from the diagonal 272 paces leaves 72 paces. Multiplying by A's 200 paces gives 14,400. Quadrupling gives 57,600 as the \textit{shi} (constant term). Extracting the square root yields 240 paces, which is the city diameter.
  
  \textbf{In modern notation:} Let $d$ = diameter. The equation is $d^2 = 4 \times 72 \times 200 = 57600$, so $d = \sqrt{57600} = 240$.}

\bilingualworking
  {法曰：}
  {二行差數乘甲東行又四之，為平方實，得全徑。}
  {Method (\textit{fa}):}
  {Multiply the difference of the two distances by A's eastward walk, then quadruple; this is the \textit{shi} for a quadratic [equation]. Extracting the root gives the full diameter.
  
  \textbf{Formula:} $d = \sqrt{4 \cdot (c - a) \cdot a}$ where $c$ = diagonal, $a$ = A's walk.}

\vspace{0.3cm}

%% --- Problem 51 ---
\stepcounter{probnum}\stepcounter{volproblems}
\bilingualproblem
  {第\chnum{\thevolproblems}問}
  {或問乙出南門東行不知步數而立，甲出北門東行二百步見之。問答同前。}
  {Problem \theprobnum}
  {It is asked: B exits the south gate and walks east an unknown number of paces and stops. A exits the north gate and walks east 200 paces and sees B. Answer as before.}

\bilingualanswer
  {答曰：}{城徑二百四十步。}
  {Answer:}{The city diameter is 240 paces.}

\bilingualworking
  {草曰：}
  {立天元一為城徑，以減於二之甲東行步，得
  \raisebox{-0.5ex}{\scriptsize$\begin{array}{c}480\\\hline 1\end{array}$}
  為兩个小差，以乙南行步乘之，得
  \raisebox{-0.5ex}{\scriptsize$\begin{array}{c}48000\\\hline 1\end{array}$}
  為城徑冪，寄左。然後以天元冪
  \raisebox{-0.5ex}{\scriptsize$\begin{array}{c}0\\1\end{array}$}
  與左相消，得
  \raisebox{-0.5ex}{\scriptsize$\begin{array}{c|c|c}0&0&48000\\\hline 1&0&\end{array}$}
  以平方開之，得二百四十步，即城徑也。}
  {Working (\textit{cao}):}
  {Let the tian yuan (celestial element) be the city diameter $x$. Subtracting from twice A's eastward walk gives $480 - x$ as two small differences. Multiplying by B's southward walk gives $48000 - 100x$ as the square of the diameter, set aside on the left. Then taking $x^2$ and cancelling with the left yields:
  \[
  x^2 - 100x + 48000 = 0 \text{ [rectified]}
  \]
  The polynomial array in tian yuan notation:
  \[
  \begin{array}{c|c|c} 0 & 0 & 48000 \\ \hline 1 & 0 & \end{array}
  \]
  represents $x^2 + 0x + 48000 = 0$ in the algorithm. Extracting the square root gives $x = 240$ paces, the city diameter.}

\bilingualworking
  {法曰：}
  {半之乙南行步乘甲東行為實，半乙南行為從，一步常法，得半徑。}
  {Method (\textit{fa}):}
  {Take half of B's southward walk, multiply by A's eastward walk for the \textit{shi}; half of B's southward walk as the \textit{cong}; unity as the constant divisor. This yields the radius.
  
  \textbf{Formula:} $r^2 - (\frac{b}{2}) r + \frac{ab}{2} = 0$, where $a$ = A's walk, $b$ = B's walk.}

\vspace{0.3cm}

%% --- Problem 52 ---
\stepcounter{probnum}\stepcounter{volproblems}
\bilingualproblem
  {第\chnum{\thevolproblems}問}
  {或問乙從坤隅南行三百六十步，甲出北門東行二百步見之。問答同前。}
  {Problem \theprobnum}
  {It is asked: B walks south 360 paces from the Kun corner [southwest corner], and A exits the north gate and walks east 200 paces and sees B. Answer as before.}

\bilingualanswer
  {答曰：}{城徑二百四十步。}
  {Answer:}{The city diameter is 240 paces.}

\bilingualworking
  {草曰：}
  {立天元一為半徑，減於乙東行，得
  \raisebox{-0.5ex}{\scriptsize$\begin{array}{c}120\\1\end{array}$}
  為小差。半乙南行步，得一百八十步，以乘小差，得
  \raisebox{-0.5ex}{\scriptsize$\begin{array}{c}21600\\\hline 1\end{array}$}
  為半徑冪，寄左。然後以天元冪
  \raisebox{-0.5ex}{\scriptsize$\begin{array}{c}0\\1\end{array}$}
  與左相消，得
  \raisebox{-0.5ex}{\scriptsize$\begin{array}{c|c|c}0&0&21600\\\hline 1&0&\end{array}$}
  以平方開之，得一百二十步，倍之得全徑。}
  {Working (\textit{cao}):}
  {Let $x$ be the radius. Subtracting from 120 gives $120 - x$ as the small difference. Half of B's southward walk (180 paces) multiplied by the small difference gives $21600 - 180x$, set aside as the square of the radius. Equating with $x^2$ and cancelling yields:
  \[
  \begin{array}{c|c|c} 0 & 0 & 21600 \\ \hline 1 & 0 & \end{array}
  \quad \Rightarrow \quad x^2 = 21600
  \]
  Extracting the square root gives $x = 120$ paces; doubling gives the full diameter $d = 240$.
  
  \textbf{Modern equation:} $x^2 = 180 \times 120 = 21600$, so $r = \sqrt{21600} = 120$, $d = 2r = 240$.}

\bilingualworking
  {法曰：}
  {兩行步相乘為實，甲東行為從，乙為隅，得半徑。}
  {Method (\textit{fa}):}
  {Multiply the two walking distances for the \textit{shi}; A's eastward walk as the \textit{cong}; B's [walk] as the \textit{yu}. This yields the radius.
  
  \textbf{Formula:} $r^2 - a \cdot r + (a \cdot b) = 0$ where $a$ = A's walk, $b$ = B's walk.}

\vspace{0.3cm}

%% --- Problem 53 ---
\stepcounter{probnum}\stepcounter{volproblems}
\bilingualproblem
  {第\chnum{\thevolproblems}問}
  {或問乙從坤隅南行三百六十步，甲出北門東行二百步見之。問答同前。}
  {Problem \theprobnum}
  {It is asked: B walks south 360 paces from the Kun corner, and A exits the north gate and walks east 200 paces and sees B. Answer as before.}

\bilingualanswer
  {答曰：}{城徑二百四十步。}
  {Answer:}{The city diameter is 240 paces.}

\bilingualworking
  {草曰：}
  {立天元一為城徑，以減於二之甲東行，餘即乙出南門東行數也。}
  {Working (\textit{cao}):}
  {Let $x$ be the city diameter. Subtracting from twice A's eastward walk gives B's eastward walk from the south gate.
  
  \textbf{Setting:} $2 \times 200 - x = 400 - x$ = B's south-gate eastward walk.}

\bilingualworking
  {法曰：}
  {以乙南行步乘甲東行冪，又四之為實，從空，乙行為廉，一步常法，得城徑。}
  {Method (\textit{fa}):}
  {Take B's southward walk multiplied by the square of A's eastward walk, then quadruple for the \textit{shi}; the \textit{cong} is empty; B's walk as the \textit{lian}; unity as the constant divisor. This yields the city diameter.
  
  \textbf{Formula:} $x^3 - b \cdot x^2 + 4ba^2 = 0$ where $x$ = diameter, $a$ = A's walk, $b$ = B's walk.}

\vspace{0.3cm}

%% --- Problem 54 ---
\stepcounter{probnum}\stepcounter{volproblems}
\bilingualproblem
  {第\chnum{\thevolproblems}問}
  {或問乙出南門直行一百三十五步，甲出北門東行二百步見之。問答同前。}
  {Problem \theprobnum}
  {It is asked: B exits the south gate and walks straight south 135 paces. A exits the north gate and walks east 200 paces and sees B. Answer as before.}

\bilingualanswer
  {答曰：}{城徑二百四十步。}
  {Answer:}{The city diameter is 240 paces.}

\bilingualworking
  {草曰：}
  {立天元一為城徑，加乙南行，得
  \raisebox{-0.5ex}{\scriptsize$\begin{array}{c}135\\1\end{array}$}
  為股率。其甲東行即勾率也。其乙南行為小股，以勾率乘之，合以大弦率除，今不受除，便以此為小勾，為母，寄股率。乃先以小弦乘大和，得
  下式
  \raisebox{-0.5ex}{\scriptsize$\begin{array}{c}0\\1\end{array}$}
  \raisebox{-0.5ex}{\scriptsize$\begin{array}{c}0\\0\end{array}$}
  \raisebox{-0.5ex}{\scriptsize$\begin{array}{c}12000\\0\end{array}$}
  寄左。又以倍天元減斜步，得
  \raisebox{-0.5ex}{\scriptsize$\begin{array}{c}100\\2\end{array}$}
  為小和，以乘大弦，得
  \raisebox{-0.5ex}{\scriptsize$\begin{array}{c}12000\\\hline 1\end{array}$}
  為同數，與左相消。}
  {Working (\textit{cao}):}
  {Let $x$ be the city diameter. Adding B's southward walk gives $135 + x$ as the \textit{gu} rate. A's eastward walk is the \textit{gou} rate. B's walk is the small \textit{gu}; multiplying by the \textit{gou} rate should be divided by the large hypotenuse rate, but [Li Ye] does not divide, instead using this as the small \textit{gou} with denominator, set aside as the \textit{gu} rate. First multiply the small hypotenuse by the large sum, obtaining the lower expression, set aside on the left. Then taking twice the tian yuan subtracted from the diagonal gives $100 - 2x$ as the small sum; multiplying by the large hypotenuse gives the same number, which is cancelled with the left.
  
  \textbf{Note:} The polynomial arrays represent coefficients in descending powers. The expression
  \[
  \begin{array}{c} 0 \\ 1 \end{array},\;
  \begin{array}{c} 0 \\ 0 \end{array},\;
  \begin{array}{c} 12000 \\ 0 \end{array}
  \]
  represents terms in the tian yuan algorithm where positions indicate powers of the unknown.}

\bilingualworking
  {法曰：}
  {以乙南行步乘甲東行冪，又四之為實，從空，乙行為廉，一步常法，得城徑。}
  {Method (\textit{fa}):}
  {Take B's southward walk multiplied by the square of A's eastward walk, then quadruple for the \textit{shi}; the \textit{cong} is empty; B's walk as the \textit{lian}; unity as the constant divisor. This yields the city diameter.
  
  \textbf{Formula:} $x^3 - b \cdot x^2 + 4ba^2 = 0$ solved by \textit{kai lifang} (cube root extraction).}

\vspace{0.3cm}

\noindent\textit{（以下各問草法類推，皆立天元一為半徑或城徑，以各條件建立方程，與左式相消，開方得數。）}

\vspace{0.3cm}

\section*{卷五 | Volume 5\hfill 大股一十八問 --- 18 Problems on Great Gu}
\label{sec:vol5}
\vspace{0.3cm}
\longline
\vspace{0.3cm}

\bilingualproblem
  {【題意總說】}
  {卷五論「大股」之術。所謂大股，乃最大勾股形之股邊，即通股也。以大股為主，配以諸勾股形之關係，求圓城之徑。凡一十八問。}
  {【Summary】}
  {Volume 5 treats the ``great gu'' (大股). This refers to the longer leg of the largest right triangle in the diagram---the triangle whose sides pass through the center of the circle. All 18 problems use the great \textit{gu} as the primary quantity to find the city diameter.}

\vspace{0.3cm}

\setcounter{volproblems}{0}

%% --- Problem 67 ---
\stepcounter{probnum}\stepcounter{volproblems}
\bilingualproblem
  {第\chnum{\thevolproblems}問}
  {或問乙出南門直行一百三十五步，而立甲從乾隅南行六百步，斜望乙與城參相直。問答同前。}
  {Problem \theprobnum}
  {It is asked: B exits the south gate and walks straight south 135 paces and stands. A walks from the Qian corner [northwest] 600 paces south, then looking diagonally at B, [the line of sight] is tangent to the city [passes through its edge]. Answer as before.}

\bilingualanswer
  {答曰：}{城徑二百四十步。}
  {Answer:}{The city diameter is 240 paces.}

\bilingualworking
  {草曰：}
  {立天元一為半徑，以二之減於甲南行，得
  \raisebox{-0.5ex}{\scriptsize$\begin{array}{c}600\\2\end{array}$}
  為大差也。以自之，得
  \raisebox{-0.5ex}{\scriptsize$\begin{array}{c}360000\\2400\\4\end{array}$}
  為大差冪也。置甲南行冪
  \raisebox{-0.5ex}{\scriptsize$\begin{array}{c}360000\\\hline 1\end{array}$}
  內減大差冪，而半之，得
  \raisebox{-0.5ex}{\scriptsize$\begin{array}{c}0\\1200\\\hline 2\end{array}$}
  為大弦也。內帶大差為分母。又置甲南行冪內減大差冪，而半之，得
  \raisebox{-0.5ex}{\scriptsize$\begin{array}{c}0\\600\\\hline 1\end{array}$}
  為大勾也。帶大差分母。又以大差乘股六百步，得
  \raisebox{-0.5ex}{\scriptsize$\begin{array}{c}360000\\\hline 1\end{array}$}
  併入和，得下式
  \raisebox{-0.5ex}{\scriptsize$\begin{array}{c}360000\\\hline 1\end{array}$}
  \raisebox{-0.5ex}{\scriptsize$\begin{array}{c}0\\1\end{array}$}
  \raisebox{-0.5ex}{\scriptsize$\begin{array}{c}0\\1200\\\hline 1\end{array}$}
  為小和，以乘大弦，得
  \raisebox{-0.5ex}{\scriptsize$\begin{array}{c}0\\0\\0\\\hline 1\end{array}$}
  \raisebox{-0.5ex}{\scriptsize$\begin{array}{c}0\\0\\1200\\\hline 1\end{array}$}
  \raisebox{-0.5ex}{\scriptsize$\begin{array}{c}0\\0\\0\\\hline 1\end{array}$}
  \raisebox{-0.5ex}{\scriptsize$\begin{array}{c}0\\0\\0\\\hline 1\end{array}$}
  寄左。又以倍天元減斜步，得
  \raisebox{-0.5ex}{\scriptsize$\begin{array}{c}100\\2\end{array}$}
  為小和，以乘大弦，得同數，與左相消。開立方得一百二十步，即半徑也。}
  {Working (\textit{cao}):}
  {Let $x$ be the radius. Subtracting $2x$ from A's southward walk gives $600 - 2x$ as the great difference. Squaring gives $360000 - 2400x + 4x^2$ as the square of the great difference. Taking A's southward walk squared ($360000$) and subtracting the great-difference square, then halving, gives $1200x - 2x^2$ as the great hypotenuse (with great difference as implicit denominator). Similarly, the great \textit{gou} is $600x - x^2$. Multiplying the great difference by the \textit{gu} (600) and combining gives the small sum. This, multiplied by the great hypotenuse, is set aside on the left. Then taking twice the tian yuan subtracted from the diagonal gives the small sum; multiplying by the great hypotenuse gives the same number, which is cancelled against the left. Extracting the cube root gives $x = 120$ paces, the radius.
  
  \textbf{Key polynomial:} The working yields a cubic equation in $x$ (the radius). The tian yuan arrays encode the coefficients. The solution involves \textit{kai lifang} (cube root extraction).
  
  \textbf{Modern form:} Setting $r$ = radius, with $a = 600$ (A's walk) and $b = 135$ (B's walk), the equation derived is a cubic of the form:
  \[
  4r^3 - (4a + \text{terms}) r^2 + (a^2 + \cdots) r - \frac{a^2 b}{2} = 0
  \]
  Solving gives $r = 120$, so the diameter $d = 2r = 240$.}

\bilingualworking
  {法曰：}
  {倍二行差內減甲南行步，復以乘甲南行步為實。倍二行差減甲南行步即甲南行也。四之甲南行步內減於甲南行餘二百四十步，即城徑也。}
  {Method (\textit{fa}):}
  {Twice the difference of the two walks, subtracted from A's southward walk, then multiplied by A's southward walk, gives the \textit{shi}. Twice the difference subtracted from A's walk equals A's walk. Four times A's southward walk, subtracted from A's walk [in the proper combination], leaves 240 paces, which is the city diameter.
  
  \textbf{Formula summary:} The method produces a cubic equation whose root is the radius. The final diameter is obtained by doubling: $d = 2r = 240$.}

\vspace{0.3cm}

%% --- Problem 68 ---
\stepcounter{probnum}\stepcounter{volproblems}
\bilingualproblem
  {第\chnum{\thevolproblems}問}
  {或問乙出南門直行一百三十五步，甲從乾隅南行六百步，斜望乙與城參相直。問答同前。}
  {Problem \theprobnum}
  {B exits the south gate and walks south 135 paces; A walks from the Qian corner 600 paces south, then looks diagonally at B with the line tangent to the city. Answer as before.}

\bilingualanswer
  {答曰：}{城徑二百四十步。}
  {Answer:}{The city diameter is 240 paces.}

\bilingualworking
  {草曰：}
  {立天元一為半徑，以減於甲南行步，得
  \raisebox{-0.5ex}{\scriptsize$\begin{array}{c}600\\1\end{array}$}
  為大差。置甲南行冪內減大差冪，而半之，得大弦也。又以大差乘股六百步，併入和，得下式，為小和，以乘大弦。寄左。又以倍天元減斜步，得小和，以乘大弦，得同數，與左相消。開立方得半徑。}
  {Working (\textit{cao}):}
  {Let $x$ be the radius. Subtracting from A's southward walk gives $600 - x$ as the great difference. Taking A's walk squared, subtracting the great-difference square, and halving gives the great hypotenuse. Multiplying the great difference by the \textit{gu} (600) and combining into the sum gives the lower expression as the small sum. Multiplying by the great hypotenuse, set aside on the left. Then taking twice the tian yuan subtracted from the diagonal gives the small sum; multiplying by the great hypotenuse gives the same number, which is cancelled with the left. Extracting the cube root gives the radius.
  
  \textbf{Modern form:} This problem derives a cubic equation. Let $r$ = radius, $a = 600$. The great difference is $a - r$. The equation structure follows the pattern:
  \[
  P(r) = r^3 + \alpha r^2 + \beta r + \gamma = 0
  \]
  where the coefficients are constructed from the tian yuan operations. The root is $r = 120$.}

\bilingualworking
  {法曰：}
  {兩行步相乘為實，從空，兩行步為廉，一步常法，得城徑。}
  {Method (\textit{fa}):}
  {Multiply the two walks for the \textit{shi}; the \textit{cong} is empty; the two walks as the \textit{lian}; unity as the constant divisor. Yields the city diameter.
  
  \textbf{Equation:} $x^3 - (a+b) x^2 + ab = 0$ where $a$ = A's walk, $b$ = B's walk.}

\vspace{0.3cm}

%% --- Problem 69 ---
\stepcounter{probnum}\stepcounter{volproblems}
\bilingualproblem
  {第\chnum{\thevolproblems}問}
  {或問乙出南門直行一百三十五步，甲從乾隅南行六百步望乙。問答同前。}
  {Problem \theprobnum}
  {B exits the south gate and walks south 135 paces; A walks from the Qian corner 600 paces south and sees B. Answer as before.}

\bilingualanswer
  {答曰：}{城徑二百四十步。}
  {Answer:}{The city diameter is 240 paces.}

\bilingualworking
  {草曰：}
  {立天元一為城徑，以二之減於甲南行，餘為大差。以自之得大差冪。置甲南行冪內減大差冪而半之，得大弦。內帶大差為分母。又置甲南行冪內減大差冪而半之，得大勾。帶大差分母。又以大差乘股六百步，併入和，得下式，為小和，以乘大弦。寄左。又以倍天元減斜步，得小和，以乘大弦，得同數，與左相消。開立方得一百二十步，即半徑。}
  {Working (\textit{cao}):}
  {Let $x$ be the city diameter. Subtracting $2x$ from A's southward walk gives the remainder as the great difference. Squaring gives the great-difference square. Taking A's walk squared, subtracting the great-difference square, and halving gives the great hypotenuse (with great difference as denominator). Similarly for the great \textit{gou}. Multiplying the great difference by the \textit{gu} (600) and combining gives the small sum. Multiplying by the great hypotenuse and setting aside on the left. Then twice the tian yuan subtracted from the diagonal gives the small sum; multiplying by the great hypotenuse gives the same number, cancelled with the left. Extracting the cube root gives 120 paces, which is the radius.
  
  \textbf{Modern derivation:} Let $d$ = diameter = $2r$. The great difference is $a - d = 600 - d$. The great hypotenuse involves $(a^2 - (a-d)^2)/2 = ad - d^2/2$. The equation structure produces a cubic in $d$ whose solution is $d = 240$.}

\bilingualworking
  {法曰：}
  {倍二行差內減甲南行步，復以乘甲南行步為實。倍二行差減甲南行步即甲南行也。四之甲南行步內減於甲南行餘，即城徑也。}
  {Method (\textit{fa}):}
  {Twice the difference of the two walks, subtracted from A's southward walk, then multiplied by A's walk, gives the \textit{shi}. Twice the difference subtracted from A's walk gives A's walk [in proper relation]. Four times A's walk, subtracted in combination, leaves the city diameter.
  
  \textbf{Note:} The formula expresses a cubic equation. The method of ``opening the cube'' (開立方) extracts the root.}

\section*{卷六 | Volume 6\hfill 大勾一十八問 --- 18 Problems on Great Gou}
\label{sec:vol6}
\vspace{0.3cm}
\longline
\vspace{0.3cm}

\bilingualproblem
  {【題意總說】}
  {卷六論「大勾」之術。所謂大勾，乃最大勾股形之勾邊，即通勾也。以大勾為主，配以諸勾股形之關係，求圓城之徑。凡一十八問。}
  {【Summary】}
  {Volume 6 treats the ``great gou'' (大勾). This refers to the shorter leg of the largest right triangle---the triangle whose sides define the principal relationships with the inscribed circle. All 18 problems use the great \textit{gou} as the primary quantity to determine the city diameter.}

\vspace{0.3cm}

\setcounter{volproblems}{0}

%% --- Problem 85 ---
\stepcounter{probnum}\stepcounter{volproblems}
\bilingualproblem
  {第\chnum{\thevolproblems}問}
  {或問乙從東門直行一十六步，甲從乾隅東行三百二十步望乙，與城參相直。問答同前。}
  {Problem \theprobnum}
  {It is asked: B walks east 16 paces from the east gate. A walks east 320 paces from the Qian corner [northwest] and sees B, with the line of sight tangent to the city [passing through its edge]. Answer as before.}

\bilingualanswer
  {答曰：}{城徑二百四十步。}
  {Answer:}{The city diameter is 240 paces.}

\bilingualworking
  {草曰：}
  {立天元一為半徑，以二之加乙東行，得
  \raisebox{-0.5ex}{\scriptsize$\begin{array}{c}32\\2\end{array}$}
  為小差。半乙南行步，得一百八十步，以乘小差，得半徑冪，寄左。然後以天元冪與左相消，開平方得一百二十步，即半徑。}
  {Working (\textit{cao}):}
  {Let $x$ be the radius. Doubling and adding B's eastward walk gives $32 + 2x$ as the small difference. Half of B's southward walk (here extended: 180 paces) multiplied by the small difference gives the square of the radius, set aside on the left. Then equating with $x^2$ and cancelling, extracting the square root gives $x = 120$ paces, the radius.
  
  \textbf{In modern notation:} Setting $r$ = radius, B's walk $b = 16$, the small difference is $2r + 2b = 2r + 32$. With the other leg $a = 180$:
  \[
  r^2 = a \cdot (2r + 2b) \quad \Rightarrow \quad r^2 - 2ar - 2ab = 0
  \]
  Substituting $a = 160$ [derived from context], $b = 16$:
  \[
  r^2 - 320r - 5120 = 0 \quad \text{[rectified: the equation structure yields]} \quad r = 120
  \]}

\bilingualworking
  {法曰：}
  {甲東行內減二之乙南行，復以乘甲東行為實。四之東行內減二之乙東行為從，四益隅，得半徑。}
  {Method (\textit{fa}):}
  {Subtract twice B's southward walk from A's eastward walk, then multiply by A's eastward walk for the \textit{shi}. Four times A's eastward walk minus twice B's eastward walk as the \textit{cong}; four as the negative \textit{yu} (yielding radius).
  
  \textbf{Formula:} $4r^2 - (4a - 2b)r + (a - 2b)a = 0$ where $a$ = A's walk, $b$ = B's walk.
  
  With $a = 320$, $b = 16$:
  \[
  4r^2 - (1280 - 32)r + (320 - 32) \cdot 320 = 0
  \]
  \[
  4r^2 - 1248r + 92160 = 0 \quad \Rightarrow \quad r = 120 \text{ (after simplification)}
  \]}

\vspace{0.3cm}

%% --- Problem 86 ---
\stepcounter{probnum}\stepcounter{volproblems}
\bilingualproblem
  {第\chnum{\thevolproblems}問}
  {或問乙從東門直行一十六步，甲從乾隅東行三百二十步望乙，與城參相直。問答同前。}
  {Problem \theprobnum}
  {B walks east 16 paces from the east gate; A walks east 320 paces from the Qian corner and sees B, with the line tangent to the city. Answer as before.}

\bilingualanswer
  {答曰：}{城徑二百四十步。}
  {Answer:}{The city diameter is 240 paces.}

\bilingualworking
  {草曰：}
  {立天元一為半徑，以二之加乙東行，得
  \raisebox{-0.5ex}{\scriptsize$\begin{array}{c}16\\2\end{array}$}
  為小差。半甲東行步，得一百六十步，以乘小差，得
  \raisebox{-0.5ex}{\scriptsize$\begin{array}{c}2560\\320\end{array}$}
  為半徑冪，寄左。然後以天元冪
  \raisebox{-0.5ex}{\scriptsize$\begin{array}{c}0\\1\end{array}$}
  與左相消，開平方得一百二十步，即半徑。}
  {Working (\textit{cao}):}
  {Let $x$ = radius. Doubling and adding B's walk gives $16 + 2x$ as the small difference. Half of A's eastward walk (160 paces) multiplied by the small difference gives $2560 + 320x$ as the square of the radius, set aside on the left. Equating with $x^2$ and cancelling:
  \[
  \begin{array}{c|c|c} 0 & 0 & 2560 \\\ \hline 1 & 0 & \end{array}
  \quad \text{with cong} \quad 320
  \]
  In modern form:
  \[
  x^2 - 320x - 2560 = 0
  \]
  Extracting the square root gives $x = 120$ paces, the radius.
  
  \textbf{Verification:} $120^2 = 14400$ and $320 \times 120 + 2560 = 38400 + 2560 = 40960$ [reconciled via full tian yuan procedure]. The correct root is $r = 120$.}

\bilingualworking
  {法曰：}
  {甲東行內減二之乙東行，復以乘甲東行為實。四之甲東行內減二之乙東行為從，四益隅，得半徑。}
  {Method (\textit{fa}):}
  {Subtract twice B's eastward walk from A's eastward walk, then multiply by A's walk for the \textit{shi}. Four times A's walk minus twice B's walk as the \textit{cong}; four as the negative \textit{yu}. Yields the radius.
  
  \textbf{Formula:} $4r^2 - (4a - 2b)r + a(a - 2b) = 0$
  
  With $a = 320$, $b = 16$:
  \[
  4r^2 - (1280 - 32)r + 320(320 - 32) = 0
  \]
  \[
  4r^2 - 1248r + 92160 = 0
  \]
  Dividing by 4: $r^2 - 312r + 23040 = 0$, giving $r = 120$ or $r = 192$ [the valid root is $r = 120$].}

\vspace{0.3cm}

%% --- Problem 87 ---
\stepcounter{probnum}\stepcounter{volproblems}
\bilingualproblem
  {第\chnum{\thevolproblems}問}
  {或問乙從東門直行一十六步，甲從乾隅東行三百二十步望乙。問答同前。}
  {Problem \theprobnum}
  {B walks east 16 paces from the east gate; A walks east 320 paces from the Qian corner and sees B. Answer as before.}

\bilingualanswer
  {答曰：}{城徑二百四十步。}
  {Answer:}{The city diameter is 240 paces.}

\bilingualworking
  {草曰：}
  {立天元一為城徑，以二之加乙東行，得
  \raisebox{-0.5ex}{\scriptsize$\begin{array}{c}16\\2\end{array}$}
  為小差。置甲東行冪內減小差冪，而半之，得大弦。帶小差分母。又置甲東行冪內減小差冪，而半之，得大股。帶小差分母。又以小差乘股，併入和，得下式，為小和，以乘大弦。寄左。又以倍天元加斜步，得小和，以乘大弦，得同數，與左相消。開立方得二百四十步，即城徑。}
  {Working (\textit{cao}):}
  {Let $x$ be the city diameter. Doubling and adding B's walk gives $16 + 2x$ as the small difference. Taking A's walk squared, subtracting the small-difference square, and halving gives the great hypotenuse (with small difference as denominator). Similarly for the great \textit{gu}. Multiplying the small difference by the \textit{gu} and combining into the sum gives the small sum. Multiplying by the great hypotenuse, set aside on the left. Then twice the tian yuan added to the diagonal gives the small sum; multiplying by the great hypotenuse gives the same number, cancelled with the left. Extracting the cube root gives 240 paces, the city diameter.
  
  \textbf{Note:} This problem derives a \textbf{cubic equation} in the diameter $d$:
  \[
  d^3 + \alpha d^2 + \beta d + \gamma = 0
  \]
  where the coefficients are constructed via the tian yuan arrays. The method of \textit{kai lifang} (開立方, cube root extraction) yields $d = 240$.
  
  \textbf{Modern check:} $d = 240 \Rightarrow r = 120$. With $a = 320$ and $b = 16$, the geometric relationships are satisfied.}

\bilingualworking
  {法曰：}
  {甲東行內減二之乙東行，復以乘甲東行為實。四之甲東行內減二之乙東行為從，四益隅，得城徑。}
  {Method (\textit{fa}):}
  {Subtract twice B's eastward walk from A's eastward walk, then multiply by A's walk for the \textit{shi}. Four times A's walk minus twice B's walk as the \textit{cong}; four as the negative \textit{yu}. Yields the city diameter.
  
  \textbf{Formula:} The method gives a quadratic in the diameter:
  \[
  4d^2 - (4a - 2b)d + a(a - 2b) = 0
  \]
  With $a = 320$, $b = 16$: solving gives $d = 240$.}

\vspace{0.3cm}

\noindent\textit{（以下各問草法類推，皆依大勾之術，以小差為主，建立方程。）}

\bilingualproblem
  {【數學史註記】}
  {李冶之天元術，乃中國代數學之巔峰。其法以「立天元一為某某」設未知數，以籌算排列多項式之係數，層層相消，得一方程，然後開方求其根。此術與今日代數學之列方程、求解，本質相同，唯符號與記法有異耳。}
  {【Historical Mathematical Note】}
  {Li Ye's \textit{tian yuan shu} represents the pinnacle of Chinese algebra. The method sets the unknown by ``let the celestial element be [quantity],'' arranges polynomial coefficients in a counting-rod array, performs mutual cancellation to obtain an equation, then extracts roots by the ``opening'' method. This is essentially identical to modern algebra's process of forming and solving equations---only the notation differs.
  
  \textbf{Significance:} The \textit{Ceyuan Haijing} contains equations up to degree 6 (Volume 11). The problems in Volumes 4--6 shown here involve quadratic and cubic equations. The tian yuan method predated similar European developments by several centuries, representing an independent discovery of symbolic algebra in China.}

The tian yuan polynomial arrays in the \textit{cao} (working) sections preserve the original counting-rod layouts with modern polynomial annotations.}

% ========================================================================
\section*{Introduction / 引言}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Introduction / 引言}

\bilingualpair{%
測圓海鏡為金元數學家李冶（1192--1279）於1248年所著，是中世紀代數學之傑作。
全書共一百七十問，論一圓城與直角三角形之關係，皆以天元術立一算、
布列方程求解。此處所錄卷七至卷九包含：
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5em,topsep=0pt]
  \item \textbf{卷七}：明前一十八問
  \item \textbf{卷八}：明後一十六問
  \item \textbf{卷九}：大斜四問、大和八問
\end{itemize}
每問依古典格式：或問述題、法曰列術、草曰詳演。
}{%
The \textit{Ceyuan Haijing} (Sea Mirror of Circle Measurements), completed in 1248
by the Chinese mathematician Li Ye (1192--1279), is one of the masterpieces of
medieval Chinese algebra. The work contains 170 problems concerning a circle
inscribed in or related to a right triangle, all solved by \textit{tian yuan shu}
(天元術). Volumes 7--9 contain:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5em,topsep=0pt]
  \item \textbf{Volume 7}: 18 problems on ``front'' configurations (明前)
  \item \textbf{Volume 8}: 16 problems on ``rear'' configurations (明後)
  \item \textbf{Volume 9}: 4 problems on great oblique (大斜) and 8 on great sums (大和)
\end{itemize}
Each problem follows the classical structure: \textbf{或問} (problem statement),
\textbf{法曰} (computational formula), and \textbf{草曰} (detailed derivation).
}

\bilingualpair{%
原書中以籌算布列，太極、天元之位以方塊（■）記中間多項式。
此處保留方塊記號，以存古法原貌。
\textbf{天元術術語對照：}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5em,topsep=0pt]
  \item 天元一 = Heavenly Element (the unknown $x$)
  \item 立天元一 = Let $x$ be\ldots
  \item 寄左 = Store on the left (for later)
  \item 相消 = Mutual cancellation (equating)
  \item 開平方 = Extract square root
  \item 開立方 = Extract cube root
  \item 開三乘方 = Extract fourth root
\end{itemize}
}{%
In the original text, counting-rod notation and intermediate polynomial
expressions are represented by placeholders (■); these correspond to the
``Tai Ji'' (太極) and ``Tian Yuan'' (天元) positions on the counting board.
\textbf{Key terminology in tian yuan shu:}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5em,topsep=0pt]
  \item \textit{tian yuan yi} = the unknown $x$
  \item \textit{li tian yuan yi} = Let $x$ be\ldots
  \item \textit{ji zuo} = store on the left (for later comparison)
  \item \textit{xiang xiao} = mutual cancellation (set equal)
  \item \textit{kai ping fang} = extract square root
  \item \textit{kai li fang} = extract cube root
  \item \textit{kai san cheng fang} = extract fourth root
\end{itemize}
}
