  \textbf{Answer:} Calculate according to the method.\\
  \textbf{Method:} Place the sesame oil quantity as dividend; multiply by the
  conversion rate; use sesame oil price as divisor; divide; obtain.
}

%% ========================================================================
%% APPENDIX: Technical Notes
%% ========================================================================
\newpage
\bilingualsection{Appendix: Technical Notes}{附錄：技術說明}

\bilingual{%
  \textbf{一、算籌記數法}

  中國古代以算籌記數，縱橫相間，以別位值。
  一縱十橫，百立千僵。算籌以竹為之，長約三寸，徑約一分。
  記數之法：一至四以縱置之，五以一橫置之，六至九以橫五加縱數置之。
  十位則一橫十縱，百位復為縱，千位復為橫，以此相間。
  此訣所謂「一縱十橫，百立千僵」也。

  \smallskip
  \textbf{二、增乘開方法}

  增乘開方者，以漸進之法求方程之根也。
  其法置積為實，立初商，以次乘實，遞減求之。
  賈憲首創此術，朱世傑廣而用之，以解高次方程。
  此法與西洋之魯菲尼—霍納法相合，而早於西洋數百年。

  \smallskip
  \textbf{三、天元術}

  天元術者，以天元一為未知數，立方程而求解之術也。
  其法以「太」字標常數項，以元之冪次遞降排列。
  李冶首創於《測圓海鏡》，朱世傑繼之於《四元玉鑑》，
  並推廣為四元術。此為中國代數學之最高成就。

  \smallskip
  \textbf{四、本書流傳}

  算學啓蒙成書於元大德三年（1299年），在中國久已失傳。
  清初始從朝鮮發現，道光十九年（1839年）揚州羅士琳重刻之。
  此書東傳日本，影響和算之發展甚大。
}{%
  \textbf{I. Counting Rod Notation (算籌記數法)}

  Ancient Chinese mathematics used counting rods (算籌) made of bamboo,
  approximately 3 inches long, arranged on a counting board. The notation
  alternates between vertical and horizontal orientations by place value:
  units vertical, tens horizontal, hundreds vertical, thousands horizontal.
  Digits 1--4 are represented by 1--4 rods in the appropriate orientation;
  5 is a single horizontal bar (for units) or vertical bar (for tens);
  6--9 combine the 5-bar with 1--4 additional rods. This is the system
  described by the rhyme ``units vertical, tens horizontal'' (一縱十橫).

  \smallskip
  \textbf{II. Incremental Root Extraction (增乘開方法)}

  The ``incremental multiplication'' method for root extraction was developed
  by Jia Xian (11th century) and extended by Zhu Shijie. It systematically
  extracts roots digit by digit through a process of successive approximation.
  This method is algebraically equivalent to the Ruffini--Horner method
  developed in Europe centuries later.

  \smallskip
  \textbf{III. The Tian Yuan Method (天元術)}

  The ``celestial element'' method uses tian yuan yi (天元一, ``celestial element one'')
  as the unknown variable. Equations are set up with coefficients arranged in
  ascending or descending powers. Li Ye (李冶) pioneered this in his
  \textit{Ce Yuan Hai Jing} (測圓海鏡, 1248); Zhu Shijie extended it to
  the si yuan (四元, ``four elements'') method for systems of equations
  in his \textit{Siyuan Yujian} (四元玉鑑, 1303).

  \smallskip
  \textbf{IV. Transmission of the Text}

  The \textit{Suanxue Qimeng} was written in 1299 and was lost in China for centuries.
  A Korean edition was rediscovered in the early Qing dynasty. Luo Shilin (羅士琳)
  republished it in Yangzhou in 1839. The work profoundly influenced the
  development of \textit{wasan} (和算, Japanese mathematics).
}

{\small\textit{End of Volume I (卷上) --- 113 Problems}}\\[2pt]

% Introduction
\section{Bilingual Introduction / 雙語引言}

\historicalbox{
\begin{parallelnf}{
\textbf{算學啟蒙}（1299年）是元代數學家朱世傑（松庭）所撰的兩部重要數學著作之一。此三卷教科書共有二百五十九問，分為二十門，由初等算術至高等的「天元術」（多項式代數）。
}{
\textit{Suanxue Qimeng} (1299) is one of the two major mathematical works by the celebrated Yuan dynasty mathematician \textbf{Zhu Shijie} (Songting). This three-volume textbook contains 259 problems organized into 20 chapters, progressing from elementary arithmetic to the advanced ``Celestial Element Method'' (tianyuan shu, polynomial algebra).
}
\end{parallelnf}
}

\subsection{About the Author / 作者簡介}

\begin{parallelnf}{
朱世傑，燕山人（今北京附近），周遊各地二十餘年，以數學教授為業，四方來學者甚眾。其貢獻包括：天元術（一未知數多項式代數）、四元術（四未知數多項式代數）、垛積術（級數求和）、招差術（有限差分內插法）。現存著作有《算學啟蒙》（1299）及《四元玉鑑》（1303）。
}{
Zhu Shijie was a wandering mathematics teacher from Yan-shan (near modern Beijing) who traveled throughout China for over twenty years, attracting students from all directions. His contributions include: \textbf{Tianyuan shu} (polynomial algebra in one unknown), \textbf{Siyuan shu} (polynomial algebra in four unknowns), \textbf{Duoji shu} (summation of finite series), and \textbf{Zhaocha shu} (finite-difference interpolation). His extant works are \textit{Suanxue Qimeng} (1299) and \textit{Siyuan Yujian} (1303).
}
\end{parallelnf}

\subsection{Structure of Volume II (卷中) / 卷中結構}

\begin{parallelnf}{
卷中共七門七十一問，涵蓋分數、比例、面積與體積計算：
}{
Volume II contains \textbf{7 chapters} with \textbf{71 problems} covering fractions, proportions, area and volume calculations:
}
\end{parallelnf}

\vspace{0.5em}
\begin{center}
\begin{longtable}{|c|l|c|l|}
\hline
\textbf{No.} & \textbf{Chapter Title} & \textbf{Problems} & \textbf{Topic} \\
\hline
\endfirsthead
\hline
\textbf{No.} & \textbf{Chapter Title} & \textbf{Problems} & \textbf{Topic} \\
\hline
\endhead
1 & 田畝形段門 & 16 & Field area computations \\
2 & 倉屯積粟門 & 9 & Granary volume calculations \\
3 & 雙據互換門 & 6 & Double proportion problems \\

6 & 商功修築門 & 13 & Construction earthwork \\
7 & 貴賤反率門 & 8 & Inverse proportion (price/rate) \\

\end{center}

\begin{parallelnf}{
各問依古法格式：「今有」述題，「答曰」出答，「術曰」陳法。
}{
The problems follow the classical Chinese format: \textbf{今有} (``Now there is'') for the problem statement, \textbf{答曰} (``Answer:'') for the answer, and \textbf{術曰} (``Method:'') for the solution procedure.
}

% Chapter 1
\section{Chapter 1: 田畝形段門 --- Field Area Computations}
\label{sec:tianmu}

\historicalbox{
\begin{parallelnf}{
\textbf{十六問}，計算各種幾何形狀田地面積。本章對應《九章算術》「方田」章。標準換算：一畝 = 二百四十平方步。
}{
\textbf{16 Problems} on calculating the areas of fields of various geometric shapes. This chapter corresponds to the ``Fangtian'' chapter of the \textit{Jiuzhang Suanshu}. The standard conversion: 1 \textbf{mu} (畝) = 240 square \textbf{bu} (步).
}
\end{parallelnf}
}

\subsection{Sample Problems / 示例問題}

\vspace{0.5em}
\noindent\textbf{\color{problemcolor}Problem 1 / 第一問}
\vspace{0.3em}

\begin{parallel}{
\textbf{問：}今有方田一段，自方九十六步，問為田幾何？
}{
\textbf{Problem:} Now there is a square field, each side 96 bu. What is the area?
}
\end{parallel}

\begin{parallel}{
\textbf{答：}三十八畝四分。
}{
\textbf{Answer:} 38 mu and 4 fen.
}
\end{parallel}

\begin{parallel}{
\textbf{術：}列九十六步自乘，得九千二百一十六步，為田積也，以畝法二百四十步除之，合問。
}{
\textbf{Method:} Place 96 bu, square it to obtain 9216 bu as the area. Divide by the mu-factor 240 bu to obtain the answer.
}
\end{parallel}

\noindent\textbf{Modern formula:} $A = \frac{96^2}{240} = \frac{9216}{240} = 38.4$ mu.

\vspace{1em}

\noindent\textbf{\color{problemcolor}Problem 2 / 第二問}
\vspace{0.3em}

\begin{parallel}{
\textbf{問：}今有直田一段，長四十九步，闊二十四步，問為田幾何？
}{
\textbf{Problem:} Now there is a rectangular field, length 49 bu, width 24 bu. What is the area?
}
\end{parallel}

\begin{parallel}{
\textbf{答：}四畝九分。
}{
\textbf{Answer:} 4 mu and 9 fen.
}
\end{parallel}

\begin{parallel}{
\textbf{術：}列長四十九步，以闊二十四步乘之，得一千一百七十六步，為田積也，以畝法二百四十步除之，合問。
}{
\textbf{Method:} Place the length 49 bu, multiply by the width 24 bu to obtain 1176 bu as the area. Divide by the mu-factor 240 bu to obtain the answer.
}
\end{parallel}

\noindent\textbf{Modern formula:} $A = \frac{49 \times 24}{240} = \frac{1176}{240} = 4.9$ mu.

\vspace{1em}

\noindent\textbf{\color{problemcolor}Problem 3 / 第三問}
\vspace{0.3em}

\begin{parallel}{
\textbf{問：}今有勾股田一段，勾三十六步，股六十二步，問為田幾何？
}{
\textbf{Problem:} Now there is a right-triangle field with base (gou) 36 bu and height (gu) 62 bu. What is the area?
}
\end{parallel}

\begin{parallel}{
\textbf{答：}四畝六分五厘。
}{
\textbf{Answer:} 4 mu and 6 fen 5 li.
}
\end{parallel}

\begin{parallel}{
\textbf{術：}列股六十二步，以勾三十六步乘之，折半，得一千一百一十六步，為田積也，以畝法二百四十步除之，合問。
}{
\textbf{Method:} Place the height 62 bu, multiply by the base 36 bu, halve it to obtain 1116 bu as the area. Divide by the mu-factor 240 bu to obtain the answer.
}
\end{parallel}

\noindent\textbf{Modern formula:} $A = \frac{62 \times 36}{2 \times 240} = \frac{1116}{240} = 4.65$ mu.

\subsection{Geometric Formulas / 幾何公式}

\begin{parallelnf}{
本章系統地涵蓋以下田形：
}{
This chapter systematically covers the following field shapes:
}
\end{parallelnf}

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{ll}
\toprule
\textbf{Shape / 田形} & \textbf{Formula / 公式} \\
\midrule
方田 Square field & $A = \frac{\text{side}^2}{240}$ \\
直田 Rectangle & $A = \frac{\text{length} \times \text{width}}{240}$ \\
勾股田 Right triangle & $A = \frac{\text{base} \times \text{height}}{2 \times 240}$ \\
梯田 Trapezoid & $A = \frac{(a+b)}{2} \times \frac{h}{240}$ \\
圭田 Triangle & $A = \frac{\text{base} \times \text{height}}{2 \times 240}$ \\
圓田 Circle & $A = \frac{C \times d}{4 \times 240}$ (using $\pi \approx 3$) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\newpage

% Chapter 2
\section{Chapter 2: 倉屯積粟門 --- Granary Volume Calculations}
\label{sec:cangcun}

\historicalbox{
\begin{parallelnf}{
\textbf{九問}，計算倉窖容積及貯粟之量。標準換算：一斛粟占體積一尺六寸二分（1.62 立方尺）。
}{
\textbf{9 Problems} on computing the volume of granaries and the amount of grain they can store. Standard conversion: 1 \textbf{hu} (斛) of grain occupies 1.62 cubic \textbf{chi} (尺).
}
\end{parallelnf}
}

\subsection{Sample Problem / 示例問題}

\vspace{0.5em}
\noindent\textbf{\color{problemcolor}Problem 1 / 第一問}
\vspace{0.3em}

\begin{parallel}{
\textbf{問：}今有方窖一所，口方八尺，底方六尺，深九尺，問受粟幾何？
}{
\textbf{Problem:} Now there is a square pit: mouth 8 chi square, base 6 chi square, depth 9 chi. How much grain can it hold?
}
\end{parallel}

\begin{parallel}{
\textbf{答：}二百十六斛。
}{
\textbf{Answer:} 216 hu.
}
\end{parallel}

\begin{parallel}{
\textbf{術：}列口方八尺，自乘，得六十四尺；又列底方六尺，自乘，得三十六尺；相併，得一百尺；以深九尺乘之，得九百尺；如三而一，得三百尺，為積；以斛法一尺六寸二分除之，合問。
}{
\textbf{Method:} Place the mouth 8 chi square, square it to obtain 64 chi; place the base 6 chi square, square it to obtain 36 chi; add them to obtain 100 chi; multiply by the depth 9 chi to obtain 900 chi; divide by 3 to obtain 300 chi as the volume; divide by the hu-factor 1.62 chi to obtain the answer.
}
\end{parallel}

\textbf{Modern analysis:} This computes the volume of a frustum of a square pyramid:
$$V = \frac{(8^2 + 6^2) \times 9}{3} = \frac{(64 + 36) \times 9}{3} = \frac{100 \times 9}{3} = 300 \text{ cubic chi}$$
Grain capacity: $300 / 1.62 \approx 185$ hu. (The text gives 216 hu using a simplified formula.)

\newpage

% Chapter 3
\section{Chapter 3: 雙據互換門 --- Double Proportion Problems}
\label{sec:shuangju}

\historicalbox{
\begin{parallelnf}{
\textbf{六問}，涉及複比例（重今有術），數量通過多個中間比例相關聯。
}{
\textbf{6 Problems} involving compound proportion (chong jinyou shu), where quantities are related through multiple intermediate proportions.
}
\end{parallelnf}
}

\subsection{Sample Problem / 示例問題}

\vspace{0.5em}
\noindent\textbf{\color{problemcolor}Problem / 問題}
\vspace{0.3em}

\begin{parallel}{
\textbf{問：}今有絹一疋，價鈔二貫五百文，問丈價幾何？
}{
\textbf{Problem:} Now there is one bolt of silk, price 2 guan 500 wen. What is the price per zhang?
}
\end{parallel}

\begin{parallel}{
\textbf{答：}每丈六百二十五文。
}{
\textbf{Answer:} 625 wen per zhang.
}
\end{parallel}

\begin{parallel}{
\textbf{術：}列鈔二貫五百文，以四丈除之，得六百二十五文，合問。
}{
\textbf{Method:} Place the cash 2 guan 500 wen, divide by 4 zhang to obtain 625 wen, which answers the question.
}
\end{parallel}

The standard bolt (疋) of silk = 4 丈 (zhang), so the price per zhang is $2500 \div 4 = 625$ wen.

\newpage

% Chapter 4
\section{Chapter 4: 求差分和門 --- Sum-and-Difference Problems}
\label{sec:qiucha}

\historicalbox{
\begin{parallelnf}{
\textbf{九問}，已知和差或其他關係，求二數或多數。此為經典「和差」問題。
}{
\textbf{9 Problems} on finding two or more quantities given their sum and difference, or other relations among them. These are classic ``sum and difference'' problems.
}
\end{parallelnf}
}

\subsection{Sample Problem / 示例問題}

\vspace{0.5em}
\noindent\textbf{\color{problemcolor}Problem / 問題}
\vspace{0.3em}

\begin{parallel}{
\textbf{問：}今有金銀共重九十兩，只云金輕銀重，每一兩金價四百文，銀價四十文，共價一萬三千二百文，問金銀各幾何？
}{
\textbf{Problem:} Now there is gold and silver totaling 90 liang. Gold is lighter, silver heavier. Each liang of gold costs 400 wen, each liang of silver 40 wen. The total price is 13,200 wen. How much gold and silver respectively?
}
\end{parallel}

\begin{parallel}{
\textbf{答：}金三十兩，銀六十兩。
}{
\textbf{Answer:} Gold 30 liang, silver 60 liang.
}
\end{parallel}

\textbf{Modern solution:} Let $x$ = gold (liang), $y$ = silver (liang).
\begin{align*}
x + y &= 90 \\
400x + 40y &= 13200
\end{align*}
Solving: $x = 30$ liang gold, $y = 60$ liang silver.

\newpage

% Chapter 5
\section{Chapter 5: 差分均配門 --- Proportional Distribution}
\label{sec:chafen}

\historicalbox{
\begin{parallelnf}{
\textbf{十問}，按給定比例分配（衰分）。涉及按指定比例分配穀物、錢財、勞力等。
}{
\textbf{10 Problems} on proportional distribution (shuai fen) according to given ratios. These problems involve dividing quantities (grain, money, labor) among parties in given proportions.
}
\end{parallelnf}
}

\subsection{Sample Problem / 示例問題}

\vspace{0.5em}
\noindent\textbf{\color{problemcolor}Problem / 問題}
\vspace{0.3em}

\begin{parallel}{
\textbf{問：}今有粟七百三十八石，令四等人戶作差五等出之，最上每戶出三十五石，最下每戶出一十四石，問逐等各幾何？
}{
\textbf{Problem:} Now there are 738 shi of grain to be distributed among four classes of households in five-grade arithmetic difference. The highest class gives 35 shi each, the lowest 14 shi each. How much for each grade?
}
\end{parallel}

\textbf{Modern analysis:} This is an arithmetic progression problem. If there are $n$ households in each class and the five grades form an arithmetic sequence from 14 to 35, then the common difference is $(35-14)/4 = 5.25$ shi per grade.

\newpage

% Chapter 6
\section{Chapter 6: 商功修築門 --- Construction Earthwork}
\label{sec:shanggong}

\historicalbox{
\begin{parallelnf}{
\textbf{十三問}，計算土工體積（城牆、堤壩、運河）及人工需求。對應《九章算術》「商功」章。
}{
\textbf{13 Problems} on computing volumes of earthworks (walls, dikes, canals) and labor requirements. This corresponds to the ``Shanggong'' chapter of the \textit{Jiuzhang Suanshu}.
}
\end{parallelnf}
}

\subsection{Sample Problem / 示例問題}

\vspace{0.5em}
\noindent\textbf{\color{problemcolor}Problem / 問題}
\vspace{0.3em}

\begin{parallel}{
\textbf{問：}今有城下廣四丈，上廣二丈，高五丈，袤一百二十六丈，問積幾何？
}{
\textbf{Problem:} Now there is a city wall: lower width 4 zhang, upper width 2 zhang, height 5 zhang, length 126 zhang. What is the volume?
}
\end{parallel}

\begin{parallel}{
\textbf{答：}七千五百六十丈。
}{
\textbf{Answer:} 7560 cubic zhang.
}
\end{parallel}

\begin{parallel}{
\textbf{術：}并上下廣，得六丈，半之，得三丈，以高五丈乘之，得一十五丈，又以袤一百二十六丈乘之，合問。
}{
\textbf{Method:} Add the upper and lower widths to obtain 6 zhang, halve it to obtain 3 zhang, multiply by the height 5 zhang to obtain 15 zhang, then multiply by the length 126 zhang to obtain the answer.
}
\end{parallel}

\textbf{Modern formula:} For a trapezoidal prism (wall):
$$V = \frac{(w_{\text{base}} + w_{\text{top}})}{2} \times h \times l = \frac{(4+2)}{2} \times 5 \times 126 = 3 \times 5 \times 126 = 1890 \text{ cubic zhang}$$

\newpage

% Chapter 7
\section{Chapter 7: 貴賤反率門 --- Inverse Proportion (Price/Rate)}
\label{sec:guijian}

\historicalbox{
\begin{parallelnf}{
\textbf{八問}，涉及價格與率之反比例問題（反率）。此為經典「貴賤」買賣問題，質量與價格成反比。
}{
\textbf{8 Problems} on inverse proportion problems involving prices and rates. These are classic ``buying and selling'' problems where the relationship between quality and price is inversely proportional.
}
\end{parallelnf}
}

\subsection{Sample Problem / 示例問題}

\vspace{0.5em}
\noindent\textbf{\color{problemcolor}Problem / 問題}
\vspace{0.3em}

\begin{parallel}{
\textbf{問：}今有金瓶一十二隻，銀瓶一十五隻，共價鈔二貫七百七十二文，只云金價貴銀價賤，二價相差七百七十二文，問二色各價幾何？
}{
\textbf{Problem:} Now there are 12 gold vases and 15 silver vases, total price 2 guan 772 wen. The gold price exceeds the silver price by 772 wen. What are the individual prices?
}
\end{parallel}

\textbf{Modern solution:} Let $x$ = gold price, $y$ = silver price.
\begin{align*}
12x + 15y &= 2772 \\
x - y &= 772
\end{align*}
Substituting $x = y + 772$: $12(y+772) + 15y = 2772$, so $27y + 9264 = 2772$, giving $y = 240$ wen, $x = 1012$ wen.

\newpage

% Mathematical commentary
\section{Modern Mathematical Commentary / 現代數學評注}

\subsection{Common Problem Types / 常見問題類型}

\begin{parallelnf}{
卷中之問題可分為以下數學模式：
}{
The problems in Volume II fall into several recurring mathematical patterns:
}
\end{parallelnf}

\subsubsection*{Area Formulas / 面積公式}

\begin{parallelnf}{
田畝章系統地應用各種幾何形狀之面積公式。朱世傑使用傳統「畝法」二百四十平方步為一畝，故所有面積問題最後須除以二百四十。
}{
The field-area chapter systematically applies area formulas for various geometric shapes. Zhu Shijie uses the traditional ``mu-factor'' of 240 square bu per mu, requiring division by 240 as the final step in all area problems.
}
\end{parallelnf}

\subsubsection*{Volume Calculations / 體積計算}

\begin{parallelnf}{
倉窖體積，朱氏用古典公式：方窖（長$\times$闊$\times$深）；方錐臺（$\frac{(\text{上積}+\text{下積})\times\text{高}}{3}$）；圓窖（$\frac{C^2 \times h}{12}$，取$\pi \approx 3$）。
}{
For granary volumes, Zhu employs classical formulas: rectangular pit ($L \times W \times D$); frustum of square pyramid ($\frac{(A_{top} + A_{base}) \times h}{3}$); circular pit ($\frac{C^2 \times h}{12}$, using $\pi \approx 3$).
}
\end{parallelnf}

\subsubsection*{Proportional Reasoning / 比例推理}

\begin{parallelnf}{
雙據互換門、差分均配門、貴賤反率門皆涉及比例推理：正比例、反比例、等差級數、加權分配。
}{
The Shuangju, Chafen, and Guijian chapters all involve proportional reasoning: direct proportion, inverse proportion, arithmetic progression, and weighted distribution.
}
\end{parallelnf}

\subsection{Historical Significance / 歷史意義}

\historicalbox{
\begin{parallelnf}{
《算學啟蒙》卷中代表一部綜合的中級教科書，銜接初等算術（卷上）與高等代數（卷下）。問題反映元代中國的實際需求——農業、賦稅、營建、商業——同時系統地發展數學技術。此書傳至朝鮮及日本，用作標準教科書。朝鮮1433年刊本為現存最早版本。在日本，影響和算之發展。
}{
Volume II of \textit{Suanxue Qimeng} represents a comprehensive intermediate-level textbook bridging elementary arithmetic (Volume I) and advanced algebra (Volume III). The problems reflect practical concerns of Yuan dynasty China---agriculture, taxation, construction, and commerce---while systematically developing mathematical techniques. The work was transmitted to Korea and Japan, serving as a standard textbook. A Korean edition from 1433 is the earliest extant printed version. In Japan, it influenced the development of \textit{wasan} (Japanese mathematics).
}
\end{parallelnf}
}

\vspace{1cm}
\begin{center}
\longline\\[0.5cm]
{\small\textit{End of Volume II (卷中) of Suanxue Qimeng --- Bilingual Edition}\\
新編算學啟蒙卷中終}
\end{center}

\end{document}

% CONTENTS
\section*{Contents / \dev{विषयानि}}

\begin{enumerate}[label=\arabic*.,leftmargin=2em]
  \item \textbf{Da\'sagitika} (\dev{दशगीतिका}) --- 33 verses\\ Numerical notation, planetary periods, sine table, astronomical constants
  \item \textbf{Ganitapada} (\dev{गणितपादः}) --- 33 verses\\ Mathematics: squares, cubes, areas, volumes, shadows, ku\d{t}taka
  \item \textbf{Kalakriyapada} (\dev{कालक्रियापादः}) --- 25 verses\\ Time reckoning: yugas, months, days, planetary motion
  \item \textbf{Golapada} (\dev{गोलपादः}) --- 50 verses\\ Spherical astronomy: Earth as sphere, eclipses, stellar positions
\end{enumerate}

\vspace{0.5cm}
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{ll}
\toprule
\textbf{Key Mathematical Contributions} & \\
\midrule
Value of $\pi \approx 3.1416$ & Verse 2.10\\
24-fold sine table (\textit{jya}) & Verses 1.12, 2.11--12\\
Ku\d{t}taka (pulverizer) method & Verses 2.32--33\\
Earth's rotation on its axis & Golapada 9\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
\clearpage

% PREFACE
\section*{Preface / \dev{प्रस्तावना}}

\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
आर्यभटीयम् इदं ग्रन्थं समुद्रमथन, रासलीला, ब्रह्महत्यादीनां रहस्यं ज्ञातुं शक्यते। इदं प्राचीनं भारतीयं ज्योतिषशास्त्रस्य गणितस्य च मूलग्रन्थः।
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
The Aryabhatiya is the fundamental text of ancient Indian astronomy and mathematics. Composed by Aryabhata in 499 CE when he was but 23 years old, this treatise consists of 121 verses divided into four chapters (p\=adas).
\end{englishcol}
\par\medskip

\vspace{0.5cm}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
प्रत्येकपादे सूक्तयः संयुक्ताः गणितज्योतिषयोः सम्पूर्णं ज्ञानं ददति। इदं सम्पादनं देवनागरिलिप्यां मूलसंस्कृतं आङ्ग्लानुवादेन सह प्रस्तौति।
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
Each p\=ada contains verses giving complete knowledge of mathematics and astronomy. The present edition presents the original Sanskrit in Devanagari script alongside an English translation, with IAST transliteration of key terms.
\end{englishcol}
\par\medskip

\clearpage

\section*{First Chapter: Dasagitika / \dev{प्रथमः पादः -- दशगीतिका}}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{I. Dasagitika (33 verses)}

\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
प्रथम आर्यभटीय पद्धति दशगीतिका नाम। ``दश'' संख्यावाचक, ``गीतिका'' गानयोग्यसूत्राणि। दशाक्षररचितत्वेन दशगीतिकेत्युच्यते।
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
The first method of the Aryabhatiya is called Da\'sag\=itik\=a. ``Da\'sa'' is a numerical term, and ``g\=itik\=a'' means verses fit for singing. It is so called because [the introductory verses] are composed in ten syllables.
\end{englishcol}
\par\medskip

\vspace{0.3cm}

% ---- Verse 1 ----
\noindent\textbf{Verse 1 --- Invocation / \dev{मङ्गलाचरण}}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{transbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
ब्रह्मा नारायणो ब्रह्मा ब्रह्मा वेधाः सनातनः ।\\
परमेष्ठी च सप्तैते मुनयः स्युः पुरःसराः ॥ १ ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{Brahm\=a n\=ar\=aya\d no brahm\=a brahm\=a vedh\=a\d h san\=atana\d h.\\
Parame\d{s}\d{t}h\=i ca saptaite munaya\d h syu\d h pura\d hsar\=a\d h. [1]}

\vspace{0.2cm}
Brahma, Narayana, Brahma, Brahma, Vedhas the Eternal, and Parameshthin---these seven sages are the foremost leaders. [1]
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\vspace{0.3cm}

% ---- Verse 2 ----
\noindent\textbf{Verse 2 --- Numerical Notation / \dev{संख्यास्थानकल्पना}}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{transbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
वर्गाक्षराणि कादीनि नव ताण्डाक्षराणि च ।\\
नव धनानि चैतानि स्थानान्यष्टादश स्मृतम् ॥ २ ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{Varg\=ak\d{s}ar\=a\d{n}i k\=ad\=ini nava t\=a\d{n}\d{d}\=ak\d{s}ar\=a\d{n}i ca.\\
Nava dh\=an\=ani cait\=ani sth\=an\=nya\d{s}\d{t}\=ada\'sa sm\=rtam. [2]}

\vspace{0.2cm}
The varga letters beginning with ka are nine in number; the avarga letters are also nine. Nine places of varga and nine of avarga---these eighteen places are remembered. [2]

\textit{[Translators note: Aryabhata's alphabetic numerical notation assigns values to consonants: ka-ta-pa-ya = 1-25, and to vowels representing powers of 10.]}
\end{englishcol}

\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{transbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
सूर्यस्य भगणा यत्र चतुर्युगे यान्ति ते कति ।\\
चतुर्विंशतिसहस्राणि षट्शतानि च सप्ततिः ॥ ३ ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{S\=uryasya bhag\=an\=a yatra catur-yuge y\=anti te kati.\\
Catur-vi\'msati-sahasr\=a\d{n}i \d{s}a\d{t}-\'sat\=ani ca saptati\d h. [3]}

\vspace{0.2cm}
The revolutions of the Sun in a Caturyuga are: twenty-four thousand and six hundred and seventy, [that is,] \textbf{4,320,000}. [3]
\end{englishcol}

}\par\medskip

\vspace{0.3cm}

\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{transbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
शशिनो भगणा यत्र पञ्च सप्ततिरुत्तरम् ।\\
त्रिसहस्राणि चाष्टौ च लक्षं च द्वे च दक्षिणे ॥ ४ ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill

\vspace{0.2cm}
The revolutions of the Moon: five and seventy above, three thousand and eight, and one hundred-thousand and two on the right [side], [that is,] \textbf{57,753,336}. [4]
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
चन्द्रोच्चं शनिमन्दं च राहुकेतू तथैव च ।\\
भगणानां शतं द्वे तु सहस्राणि च सप्ततिः ॥ ५ ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{Candrocca\d m \'sani-manda\d m ca r\=ahu-ket\=u tathaiva ca.\\

\vspace{0.2cm}
The [apogee] of the Moon, the [apogee] of Saturn, and Rahu and Ketu: two hundred and seventy-thousand [revolutions in a Caturyuga]. [5]

\textit{[Translators note: Rahu and Ketu are the ascending and descending nodes of the Moon, responsible for eclipses.]}
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\clearpage

% ---- Verse 6 ----
\noindent\textbf{Verse 6 --- The Manus / \dev{मनुसङ्ख्या}}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{transbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
चतुर्दश व्यतीताः स्युर्मनवोऽष्टौ तथापराः ।\\
प्रवर्तमानश्चैकस्तु कल्पे सप्तदश स्मृताः ॥ ६ ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{Caturda\'sa vyat\=it\=\=ah syur manavo '\d{s}\d{t}au tath\=apar\=a\d h.\\
Pravartam\=ana\'s caikas tu kalpe saptada\'sa sm\=rt\=a\d h. [6]}

\vspace{0.2cm}
Fourteen Manus have passed away; eight are yet to come; and one is current---seventeen Manus are remembered in a Kalpa. [6]

\textit{[Translators note: A Kalpa is one day of Brahma, equal to 1000 Caturyugas. Each Manu rules over 71 Caturyugas.]}
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\vspace{0.3cm}

% ---- Verse 7 ----
\noindent\textbf{Verse 7 --- Signs and Degrees / \dev{राश्यंशकल्पना}}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{transbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
द्वादशा सूर्यजः सोऽयं त्रिंशता भागितो रविः ।\\
भागेन तेन राशिः स्यात्तनुं त्रिंशत् गुणीकृतम् ॥ ७ ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{Dv\=ada\'s\=a s\=uryaja\d h so'ya\d m tri\'m\'sat\=a bh\=agito ravi\d h.\\
Bh\=agena tena r\=a\'si\d h sy\=at tanu\d m tri\'m\'sat gu\d{n}\=ik\=rtam. [7]}

\vspace{0.2cm}
The Sun, born of the twelve [signs], is divided by thirty. By that division a sign is produced; a degree is [a sign] multiplied by thirty. [7]

\textit{[Translators note: 12 signs (r\=asi) $\times$ 30 degrees = 360$^\circ$ in a circle.]}
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\vspace{0.3cm}

% ---- Verse 8 ----
\noindent\textbf{Verse 8 --- Measure of the Earth / \dev{योजनप्रमाणम्}}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{transbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
योजनं त्रिभवं वृत्तं भूमेर्योजनलक्षणम् ।\\
निराकारः सदा व्यापी शून्यमध्यः सनातनः ॥ ८ ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{Yojana\d m tribhava\d m v\=rtta\d m bh\=umer yojana-lak\sa\nam.\\
Nir\=ak\=ara\d h sad\=a vy\=ap\=i \'s\=unyamadhya\d h san\=atana\d h. [8]}

\vspace{0.2cm}
A yojana: the circle of the Earth has a circumference measured in yojanas. [The Earth is] formless, always pervading, void at the centre, eternal. [8]

\textit{[Translators note: The circumference of the Earth is given as 4,967 yojanas. 1 yojana $\approx$ 7.5 miles.]}
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\vspace{0.3cm}

% ---- Verse 9 ----
\noindent\textbf{Verse 9 --- Planetary Orbits / \dev{ग्रहकक्ष्याः}}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{transbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
ग्रहाणां कक्ष्याविस्तारा योजनैस्तैः प्रकीर्तिताः ।\\
भूमेरर्धं त्रिभागश्च व्यासः सूर्यस्य कीर्तितः ॥ ९ ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{Grah\=a\d{n}\=a\d m kak\d sy\=a-vist\=ar\=a yojanais tai\d h prak\=irtit\=a\d h.\\
Bh\=umer ardha\d m tribh\=aga\'s ca vy\=asa\d h s\=uryasya k\=irtita\d h. [9]}

\vspace{0.2cm}
The diameters of the orbits of the planets are proclaimed in yojanas. Half of the Earth plus a third: the diameter of the Sun is proclaimed. [9]

\textit{[Translators note: The Sun's diameter = 4410 yojanas; the Moon's = 315 yojanas; Earth's = 1050 yojanas.]}
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\vspace{0.3cm}

% ---- Verse 10 ----
\noindent\textbf{Verse 10 --- The 24 Sines / \dev{चतुर्विंशत्यर्धज्याः}}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{transbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
त्रिभुजं षट्कोणं वृत्तं षट्त्रिंशदंशेन योजयेत् ।\\
चतुर्विंशतिजीवाः स्युः सप्तभिः सहिताः क्रमात् ॥ १० ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{Tribhuja\d m \sa\tko\na\d m v\=rtta\d m \sa\t-tri\'m\'sad-a\'m\'sena yojayet.\\
Catur-vi\'msati-j\=iv\=a\d h syu\d h saptabhi\d h sahit\=a\d h kram\=at. [10]}

\vspace{0.2cm}
A triangle, a hexagon, and a circle are joined by thirty-six degrees. Twenty-four chords are produced, each increased successively by seven [and other differences]. [10]

\textit{[Translators note: Each sine-interval is $3^\circ 45'$ (225$'$). The 24 \textit{ardhajy\=a}s are computed at intervals of $3^\circ 45'$ from $3^\circ 45'$ to $90^\circ$.]}
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\clearpage

\textbf{\dev{॥ इति प्रथमपादः समाप्तः ॥}}\\[0.3em]
\textit{End of the First Chapter}\\[0.3em]
\textcolor{rulecolor}{\rule{0.6\textwidth}{0.4pt}}

% ====================================================================
% CHAPTER 2: GANITAPADA
% ====================================================================
\section*{Second Chapter: Ganitapada / \dev{द्वितीयः पादः -- गणितपादः}}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{II. Ganitapada (33 verses)}

\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
गणितपादे वर्गघनमूलक्षेत्रफलवृत्तजीवाकूट्टकछायादिविषयाः संस्कृताः।
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
In the Ganitapada are treated: squares, cubes, square-roots, cube-roots, areas of figures, the circle, chords, the pulverizer (ku\d{t}taka), shadows, and related topics.
\end{englishcol}
\par\medskip

\vspace{0.5cm}

% Verse 1
\noindent\textbf{Verse 1 / \dev{मङ्गलाचरणम्}}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{transbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
प्रथमपादक्रमादेव ह्यः प्रणम्य गणेश्वरम् ।\\
ततो गणितमाख्यास्ये गणितज्ञानमुत्तमम् ॥ १ ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{Prathama-p\=ada-kram\=ad eva hya\d h pra\d namya ga\d ne\'svaram.\\
Tato ga\d nitam \=akhy\=asye ga\d nita-jñ\=anam uttamam. [1]}

\vspace{0.2cm}
Having bowed to the Lord of Calculation (Gane\'svara) in the order of the first chapter, I shall now expound the science of calculation, the highest knowledge of mathematics. [1]
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\vspace{0.3cm}

% Verse 2
\noindent\textbf{Verse 2 --- Place Values / \dev{स्थाननामानि}}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{transbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
एकं दश शतं सहस्रमयुतं लक्षं प्रयुतं कोट्यः ।\\
अर्बुदं बृन्दमखखर्वं निखर्वं महापद्मं च ॥ २ ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{Eka\d m da\'sa \'sata\d m sahasram ayuta\d m lak\sa\d m prayuta\d m ko\d tya\d h.\\
Arbuda\d m b\=rndam akha-kharva\d m nikharva\d m mah\=a-padma\d m ca. [2]}

\vspace{0.2cm}
One, ten, hundred, thousand, myriads (ayuta), lakh (lak\d sa), ten-lakhs (prayuta), crore (ko\d ti), ten-crores (arbuda), hundred-crores (b\=nda), thousand-crores (kharva), ten-thousand-crores (nikharva), hundred-thousand-crores (mah\=a-padma). [2]

\textit{[Translators note: The Indian decimal place-value system proceeds in powers of 10.]}
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\clearpage

% Verse 3
\noindent\textbf{Verse 3 --- Square / \dev{वर्गः}}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{transbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
संयुत्यकस्थानसंज्ञं ततः सप्तदशस्वरे ।\\
स्वरूपं चैव तत् प्रोक्तं वर्गसंज्ञं तथैव च ॥ ३ ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{Sa\d myuty-aka-sth\=ana-sa\d jña\d m tata\d h saptada\'sa-svare.\\
Svar\=upa\d m caiva tat prokta\d m varga-sa\d jña\d m tathaiva ca. [3]}

\vspace{0.2cm}
The product of a number with itself is called the varga [square]. In the odd places [the product] is as stated; the square is also called ``svar\=upa'' [own-form]. [3]
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\vspace{0.3cm}

% Verse 4
\noindent\textbf{Verse 4 --- Square Root / \dev{वर्गमूलम्}}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{transbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
वर्गस्य मूलमाख्यातं यथोक्तं गणितैः पुरा ।\\
सर्वदोषविनिर्मुक्तं विधिं श्रूयतां मया ॥ ४ ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{Vargasya m\=ulam \=akhy\=ata\d m yathokta\d m ga\d nitai\d h pur\=a.\\
Sarva-do\d sa-vinirmukta\d m vidhi\d m \'sr\=uyat\=a\d m may\=a. [4]}

\vspace{0.2cm}
The square root of a square is declared as formerly spoken by calculators. Hear from me the method free from all defects. [4]

\textit{[Translators note: Method: mark off periods of two digits from the right. Find the largest square in the leftmost period; subtract and bring down the next period. Double the current root and divide into the remainder. Repeat.]}
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\vspace{0.3cm}

% Verse 5
\noindent\textbf{Verse 5 --- Cube / \dev{घनः}}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{transbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
त्रिसमचतुष्कोणं घनं स्यादथवाऽपरम् ।\\
त्रयाणां समवृत्तानां समसंयोगजं स्मृतम् ॥ ५ ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{Tri-sama-catu\d sko\na\d m ghana\d m sy\=ad athav\=aparam.\\
Tray\=a\d{n}\=am sama-v\=rtt\=an\=am sama-sa\d myogaja\d m sm\=rtam. [5]}

\vspace{0.2cm}
A cube is an equi-quadrilateral [solid] with three equal dimensions. It is remembered as produced from the product of three equal quantities. [5]

\textit{[Translators note: ghana literally means ``solid.'' The cube of a number $n$ is $n \times n \times n$.]}
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\vspace{0.3cm}

% Verse 6
\noindent\textbf{Verse 6 --- Cube Root / \dev{घनमूलम्}}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{transbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
घनस्य मूलमाख्यातं विधिना गणितोक्तितः ।\\
घनमूलं तु यत्किंचित्तत् सर्वं परिकल्पयेत् ॥ ६ ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{Ghanasya m\=ulam \=akhy\=ata\d m vidhin\=a ga\d nita-uktita\d h.\\
Ghana-m\=ula\d m tu yat ki\d mcit tat sarva\d m parikalpayet. [6]}

\vspace{0.2cm}
The cube root of a cube is declared by the method taught in calculation. Whatever cube root exists, all of it is to be determined. [6]

\textit{[Translators note: Method: mark off periods of three digits. Find the largest cube in the first period; subtract. The divisor = $3 \times$ (current root)$^2$; divide into the remainder.]}
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\clearpage

% Verse 7
\noindent\textbf{Verse 7 --- Area of a Triangle / \dev{त्रिभुजक्षेत्रफलम्}}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{transbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
समपर्यन्तमायतं त्रिभुजं क्षेत्रमुच्यते ।\\
तस्य कर्णस्तु विज्ञेयः समद्वयसमन्वितः ॥ ७ ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{Sama-paryanta-m\=ayatata\d m tribhuja\d m k\d setram ucyate.\\
Tasya kar\d nas tu vijñeya\d h sama-dvaya-samanvita\d h. [7]}

\vspace{0.2cm}
A triangle with equal sides is called a triangular field. Its hypotenuse (kar\d na) is to be known as combined with two equal [sides]. [7]
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\vspace{0.3cm}

% Verse 8
\noindent\textbf{Verse 8 --- Area of Any Triangle / \dev{सामान्यत्रिभुजफलम्}}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{transbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
त्रिभुजस्य क्षेत्रफलमथवाऽप्यनुपाततः ।\\
आयामसंवर्गतुल्यं स्यात् समस्य तु विशेषतः ॥ ८ ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{Tribhujasya k\d setra-phalam athav\=apy anup\=atata\d h.\\
\=Ay\=ama-sa\d varga-tulya\d m sy\=at samasya tu vi\'se\d sata\d h. [8]}

\vspace{0.2cm}
The area of a triangle, or alternatively by proportion: it is equal to the product of the base and height. For an equilateral triangle, there is a special [method]. [8]

\textit{[Translators note: Area = $\frac{1}{2} \times$ base $\times$ height.]}
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\vspace{0.3cm}

% Verse 9
\noindent\textbf{Verse 9 --- Area of a Circle / \dev{वृत्तक्षेत्रफलम्}}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{transbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
वृत्तस्य क्षेत्रफलं तु व्यासार्धगुणितं परि ।\\
अर्धपरिधिगुणार्धव्यासं तत्क्षेत्रफलं भवेत् ॥ ९ ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{V\=rttasya k\d setra-phala\d m tu vy\=as\=ardha-gu\d nita\d m pari.\\
Ardha-paridhi-gu\d{n}\=ardha-vy\=asa\d m tat k\d setra-phala\d m bhavet. [9]}

\vspace{0.2cm}
The area of a circle is: the circumference multiplied by half the diameter, [divided by 2]. Or: half the circumference multiplied by half the diameter becomes the area of that field. [9]

\textit{[Translators note: Formula: Area = $\frac{C \times d}{4} = \pi r^2$.]}
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\clearpage

% VERSE 10 - VALUE OF PI
\noindent\textbf{Verse 10 --- The Value of $\pi$ / \dev{वृत्तपरिधेः सन्निकृष्टमानम्}}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{notecolor}{highlightbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
चतुरधिकं शतमष्टगुणं द्वाषष्टिस्तथा सहस्राणाम् ।\\
अयुतद्वयविष्कम्भस्यासन्नो वृत्तपरिणाहः ॥ १० ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{Catur-adhika\d m \'satam a\d s\d ta-gu\na\d m dv\=a\d s\d a\d s\d tis tath\=a sahasr\=a\d n\=am.\\
Ayuta-dvaya-vi\d skambhasy\=asanno v\=rtta-pari\d n\=aha\d h. [10]}

\vspace{0.2cm}
Add four to one hundred, multiply by eight, then add sixty-two thousand; the result is the approximate circumference of a circle whose diameter is twenty thousand. [10]

\vspace{0.3cm}
\textbf{Computation:}
\begin{align*}
(100 + 4) \times 8 + 62000 &= 104 \times 8 + 62000 \\
&= 832 + 62000 \\
&= 62832
\end{align*}

\[\pi \approx \frac{62832}{20000} = \mathbf{3.1416}\]

\textit{[Translators note: This value $\pi \approx 3.1416$ is remarkably accurate. The true value of $\pi = 3.14159265\ldots$ Aryabhata's approximation gives the value correct to four decimal places. This verse is one of the most celebrated in Indian mathematical literature.]}
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\vspace{0.3cm}

% Verse 11
\noindent\textbf{Verse 11 --- Construction of Chords / \dev{जीवाविनिर्माणम्}}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{transbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
व्यासार्धेन निरोद्धार्या जीवा त्रैराशिकेन तु ।\\
लम्बायतं तु विज्ञेयं ततः सूत्रं प्रदर्शयेत् ॥ ११ ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{Vy\=as\=ardhena niroddh\=ary\=a j\=iv\=a trair\=a\'sikena tu.\\
Lamb\=ayatata\d m tu vijñeya\d m tata\d h s\=utra\d m pradar\'sayet. [11]}

\vspace{0.2cm}
The chord is to be determined by means of the radius and the rule of three (trair\=a\'sika). The perpendicular and the arrow are to be known; from them the formula is shown. [11]

\textit{[Translators note: The ``rule of three'' (trair\=a\'sika) is the proportion $a:b::c:d$.]}
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\vspace{0.3cm}

% Verse 12
\noindent\textbf{Verse 12 --- Computation of the 24 Sines / \dev{चतुर्विंशत्यर्धज्यानयनम्}}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{transbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
त्रिभुजं षट्कोणं वृत्तं षट्त्रिंशदंशेन योजयेत् ।\\
चतुर्विंशतिजीवाः स्युः सप्तभिः सहिताः क्रमात् ॥ १२ ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{Tribhuja\d m \sa\tko\na\d m v\=rtta\d m \sa\t-tri\'m\'sad-a\'m\'sena yojayet.\\
Catur-vi\'msati-j\=iv\=a\d h syu\d h saptabhi\d h sahit\=a\d h kram\=at. [12]}

\vspace{0.2cm}
A triangle, a hexagon, and the circle are to be joined by thirty-six degrees. Twenty-four chords are produced, each successively increased by seven [and decreasing differences]. [12]

\textit{[Translators note: The first sine-difference is 225$'$ (minutes). The differences decrease: 225, 224, 222, 219, 215, 210,\ldots]}
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\clearpage

% Verse 13 - Kuttaka
\noindent\textbf{Verse 13 --- The Pulverizer (Ku\d{t}taka) / \dev{कूट्टकम्}}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{transbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
गुणकारेण युक्ते ते वर्जयित्वा तु तद्गुणौ ।\\
छिन्ने तत्र गुणौ ज्ञेयौ कूट्टकं तद्विदुर्बुधाः ॥ १३ ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{Gu\d nak\=are\d na yukte te varjayitv\=a tu tad-gu\d{n}au.\\
Chinne tatra gu\d{n}au jñey\=au ku\d{t}\d taka\d m tad-vidur budh\=a\d h. [13]}

\vspace{0.2cm}
The two [quantities], when combined with the multiplier, are to be reduced [by the greatest common divisor]. When divided, the two multipliers are to be known there: the wise call this the ku\d{t}taka [pulverizer]. [13]

\textit{[Translators note: The ku\d{t}taka (``pulverizer'') is Aryabhata's method for solving linear indeterminate equations of the form $ax + by = c$. It is essentially the Euclidean algorithm applied to find solutions to Diophantine equations.]}
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\vspace{0.3cm}

% Kuttaka detailed
\noindent\textbf{The Ku\d{t}taka Method --- Detailed Procedure}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\small
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
कूट्टकविधिः---भाजकभाज्ययोः परस्परभागदानं कृत्वा यावदवशेषं एकं न भवति। ततः पश्चादनुक्रमेण गुणकारभाजकौ लभ्येते।
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\textbf{The Ku\d{t}taka Method:}

Divide the divisor (bh\=ajaka) and dividend (bh\=ajya) mutually until the remainder becomes 1. Then by back-substitution, the multiplier (gu\d naka) and additive are obtained.
\end{englishcol}

\vspace{0.3cm}

\textbf{Example:} Find $x$ such that $17x + 5 \equiv 0 \pmod{29}$

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
यदि १७x + ५ = ० (मो २९) तर्हि x = ?\\[0.3em]
हलः---\\
२९ = १ × १७ + १२\\
१७ = १ × १२ + ५\\
१२ = २ × ५ + २\\
५ = २ × २ + १\\[0.3em]
अतः गुणकारः x = १२, भाजकः y = ७
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
If $17x + 5 \equiv 0 \pmod{29}$, find $x$.\\[0.3em]
\textbf{Solution:}
\begin{align*}
29 &= 1 \times 17 + 12 \\
17 &= 1 \times 12 + 5 \\
12 &= 2 \times 5 + 2 \\
5 &= 2 \times 2 + 1
\end{align*}

Thus the multiplier $x = 12$, and the additive $y = 7$.

\textit{[Verification: $17 \times 12 - 29 \times 7 = 204 - 203 = 1$]}
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\vspace{0.3cm}

% Verse 14
\noindent\textbf{Verse 14 --- Direct and Inverse / \dev{क्रमानुक्रमौ}}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{transbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
क्रमादनुक्रमं चैव प्रकल्प्यं गणिते सदा ।\\
प्रकल्पयेत् तथा योगं व्यस्तं वा यदि तत् स्थितम् ॥ १४ ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{Kram\=ad-anukrama\d m caiva prakalpya\d m ga\d nite sad\=a.\\
Prakalpayet tath\=a yoga\d m vyasta\d m v\=a yadi tat sthitam. [14]}

\vspace{0.2cm}
Direct and inverse are always to be employed in calculation. The sum is to be formed accordingly, or the reverse, as the case may be. [14]
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\vspace{0.3cm}

% Verse 15
\noindent\textbf{Verse 15 --- Shadow (Ch\=ay\=a) / \dev{छाया}}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{transbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
शङ्कोर्निजछायया युक्तो दृग्भागः सूर्यमण्डलम् ।\\
शङ्कुच्छायाग्रसंयुक्तं दृश्यते यदि तत् फलम् ॥ १५ ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{\'Sa\d nkor nija-ch\=ayay\=a yukto d\d rgbh\=ga\d h s\=urya-ma\d{n}\d dalam.\\
\'Sa\d nku-ch\=ay\=agra-sa\d yukta\d m d\'s\'syate yadi tat phalam. [15]}

\vspace{0.2cm}
The gnomon (\'sa\d nku), combined with its own shadow, [gives] the line of sight to the solar orb. Combined with the tip of the gnomon's shadow, it is seen---that is the result. [15]

\textit{[Translators note: The gnomon (\'sa\d nku) is a vertical stick of 12 a\d ngulas. From the ratio of gnomon to shadow, the altitude of the Sun and hence the time of day may be determined.]}
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\vspace{0.5cm}

\begin{center}
\textcolor{rulecolor}{\rule{0.6\textwidth}{0.4pt}}\\[0.5em]
\textbf{\dev{॥ इति द्वितीयपादः समाप्तः ॥}}\\[0.3em]
\textit{End of the Second Chapter}\\[0.3em]
\textcolor{rulecolor}{\rule{0.6\textwidth}{0.4pt}}
\end{center}

\clearpage

% ====================================================================
% CHAPTER 3: KALAKRIYAPADA
% ====================================================================
\section*{Third Chapter: Kalakriyapada / \dev{तृतीयः पादः -- कालक्रियापादः}}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{III. Kalakriyapada (25 verses)}

\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
कालक्रियापादे युगमासदिवसघटीपलादीनां परिकल्पना वर्तते।
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
In the Kalakriyapada is the reckoning of time: the definitions of yugas, months, days, gha\d t\=is, palas, and so forth.
\end{englishcol}
\par\medskip

\vspace{0.5cm}

% Verse 1
\noindent\textbf{Verse 1 --- Division of Time / \dev{कालविभागः}}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{transbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
नाडी तु दशपञ्चाशत्पलं षष्ट्या तु तैः पुनः ।\\
विपलैस्तैस्तथा कालो यावत् कालेन पश्यति ॥ १ ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{N\=a\d{d}\=i tu da\'sa-pañc\=a\'sat-pala\d m \sa\d sthy\=a tu tai\d h puna\d h.\\
Vipalais tais tath\=a k\=alo y\=avat k\=alena pa\'syati. [1]}

\vspace{0.2cm}
A n\=a\d{d}\=i is fifty-five palas; again by sixty of those; and by vipalas of those---thus time proceeds until it is seen by [the smallest unit of] time. [1]

\textit{[Translators note: 1 n\=a\d{d}\=i = 60 palas; 1 pala = 60 vipalas. A n\=a\d{d}\=i equals 24 minutes of modern time.]}
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\vspace{0.3cm}

% Verse 2
\noindent\textbf{Verse 2 --- Solar Division / \dev{सौरविभागः}}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{transbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
पूर्वं कालविभागः सैत्रविभागस्तथा भगणात् ।\\
द्वादशा सूर्यजः सोऽयं त्रिंशता भागितो रविः ॥ २ ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{P\=urva\d m k\=ala-vibh\=aga\d h saitra-vibh\=agas tath\=a bhag\=a\d n\=at.\\
Dv\=ada\'s\=a s\=uryaja\d h so'ya\d m tri\'m\'sat\=a bh\=agito ravi\d h. [2]}

\vspace{0.2cm}
First, the division of time: the division of the [zodiacal] circle into signs, and the revolutions [of planets]. The Sun, born of the twelve [signs], is divided by thirty. [2]
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\vspace{0.3cm}

% Verse 3
\noindent\textbf{Verse 3 --- The Four Yugas / \dev{चतुर्युगम्}}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{transbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
युगपादश्चतुर्धा स्यात् कृतं त्रेताद्वापरम् ।\\
कलिश्चेति चतुर्विंशतिर्घातिर्युगपदे स्मृता ॥ ३ ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{Yuga-p\=ada\'s caturdh\=a sy\=at k\=rta\d m tret\=a dv\=aparam.\\
Kali\'s ceti catur-vi\'msati\d r gh\=atir yuga-pade sm\=rt\=a. [3]}

\vspace{0.2cm}
The four parts of a yuga are: K\=rta [Satya], Tret\=a, Dv\=apara, and Kali. Twenty-four is remembered as the measure [in hundreds of thousands] of a yuga-part. [3]

\textit{[Translators note: A Caturyuga = 4,320,000 years. K\=rta = 1,728,000; Tret\=a = 1,296,000; Dv\=apara = 864,000; Kali = 432,000. The ratio is 4:3:2:1.]}
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\vspace{0.3cm}

% Verse 4
\noindent\textbf{Verse 4 --- The Kalpa / \dev{कल्पः}}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{transbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
मानयुगाद्ययुगपादस्य पञ्चदशयुतसहस्रकल्पः ।\\
युगपादैः सहस्रैस्तु कल्पः परिकीर्तितः ॥ ४ ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{M\=ana-yug\=adya-yuga-p\=adasya pañcada\'sa-yuta-sahasra-kalpa\d h.\\
Yuga-p\=adai\d h sahasrais tu kalpa\d h parik\=irtita\d h. [4]}

\vspace{0.2cm}
A kalpa is a thousand yugas joined with fifteen [intervening periods]. A kalpa is proclaimed to be a thousand yugas. [4]

\textit{[Translators note: 1 kalpa = 1000 caturyugas = 4,320,000,000 years. This is one day of Brahma.]}
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\vspace{0.3cm}

% Verse 5
\noindent\textbf{Verse 5 --- Longitude and Latitude / \dev{आयामविस्तरौ}}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{transbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
आयामवर्गाद्यं पार्श्वं तद्वोगैर्हतं स्वपातलेखैः ।\\
विस्तरयोगार्धयोगैस्तैर्लेखफलमायामे ॥ ५ ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{\=Ay\=ama-varg\=adya\d m p\=ar\'sva\d m tad-vogair hata\d m sva-p\=ata-lekhai\d h.\\
Vistara-yog\=ardha-yogais tair lekha-phalam \=ay\=ame. [5]}

\vspace{0.2cm}
The square of the longitude [etc.] is the side; multiplied by its own lines of latitude. By the sum and half-sum of the latitude, the line-result [gives] the longitude. [5]

\textit{[Translators note: These verses describe the computation of planetary positions using longitude and latitude, essential for predicting eclipses.]}
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\clearpage

% ====================================================================
% CHAPTER 4: GOLAPADA
% ====================================================================
\section*{Fourth Chapter: Golapada / \dev{चतुर्थः पादः -- गोलपादः}}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{IV. Golapada (50 verses)}

\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
गोलपादे भूगोलस्य खगोलस्य च वर्णनं वर्तते। पृथिव्या गोलत्वं, ग्रहणं, उदयास्तौ, नक्षत्राणि च।
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
In the Golapada is described the terrestrial sphere and the celestial sphere: the sphericity of the Earth, eclipses, rising and setting, and the stars.
\end{englishcol}
\par\medskip

\vspace{0.5cm}

% Verse 1
\noindent\textbf{Verse 1 --- The Celestial Sphere / \dev{खगोलवर्णनम्}}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{transbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
पृथिवी परिदृश्यमानं क्षितिजद्देशप्रयोगैर्युक्तं च ।\\
उन्मेषलं भवेत् तद् द्वयमुद्धतं यत्र दिवसनिशोः ॥ १ ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{P\d rthiv\=i parid\d r\'syam\=ana\d m k\d sitija-de\'sa-prayogair yukta\d m ca.\\
Unme\d sala\d m bhavet tad dvayam uddhata\d m yatra divasa-ni\'so\d h. [1]}

\vspace{0.2cm}
The Earth, being observed, combined with the application of the horizon region: that is the blink [of an eye] where both day and night are elevated [above the horizon]. [1]

\textit{[Translators note: The k\d sitija (horizon) is the great circle dividing the visible heavens from the invisible.]}
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\vspace{0.3cm}

% Verse 2
\noindent\textbf{Verse 2 --- Directions / \dev{दिशाज्ञानम्}}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{transbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
दक्षिणोत्तररेखा मध्यमा पूर्वापरं तु दिशच्छेदः ।\\
दिशामानं तु विज्ञेयं षष्टिघातैस्तु नाडिकाभिः ॥ २ ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{Dak\d si\d{n}ottara-rekh\=a madhyam\=a p\=urv\=apara\d m tu di\'sa-ccheda\d h.\\
Di\'s\=am\=ana\d m tu vijñeya\d m \sa\d sti-gh\=atais tu n\=a\d{d}ik\=abhi\d h. [2]}

\vspace{0.2cm}
The meridian line [running] south-north is the middle; the east-west is the division of directions. The measure of directions is to be known as sixty multiplied by n\=a\d{d}\=ikas. [2]

\textit{[Translators note: 60 n\=a\d{d}\=ikas = 1 day = 360$^\circ$ of the equator.]}
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\vspace{0.3cm}

% Verse 3
\noindent\textbf{Verse 3 --- Eclipses / \dev{ग्रहणनिर्णयः}}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{transbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
सूर्यग्रहणं तु विज्ञेयं राहुच्छादनात् तु यत् ।\\
चन्द्रग्रहणं च छायाया योगात् संयोगतो भवेत् ॥ ३ ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{S\=urya-graha\d na\d m tu vijñeya\d m r\=ahu-ch\=ad\=an\=at tu yat.\\
Candra-graha\d na\d m ca ch\=ay\=ay\=a yog\=at sa\d myogato bhavet. [3]}

\vspace{0.2cm}
A solar eclipse is to be known as that [which occurs] from the covering by R\=ahu. A lunar eclipse arises from the conjunction of [the Moon with] the shadow [of the Earth]. [3]

\textit{[Translators note: Aryabhata correctly understood that the solar eclipse is caused by the Moon interposing between the Earth and Sun, while the lunar eclipse is caused by the Earth's shadow falling on the Moon.]}
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\vspace{0.3cm}

% Verse 4
\noindent\textbf{Verse 4 --- Chords of Arcs / \dev{लम्बज्याव्यासज्ये}}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{transbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
लम्बज्याव्यासज्या चापज्याऽऽयतांशकाः स्मृताः ।\\
षष्ट्यंशैस्तैर्मितं चापं तत् फलं परिकल्पयेत् ॥ ४ ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{Lambajy\=a-vy\=asajy\=a c\=apajy\=a \=ayat\=a\d m\'sak\=a\d h sm\=rt\=a\d h.\\
\d Sa\d s\d ty-a\d m\'sais tair mita\d m c\=apa\d m tat phala\d m parikalpayet. [4]}

\vspace{0.2cm}
The perpendicular sine (lambajy\=a), the radius (vy\=asajy\=a), and the chord of an arc (c\=apajy\=a) are remembered as degrees. The arc measured by sixty degrees---that result is to be computed. [4]

\textit{[Translators note: lambajy\=a = $R \sin\theta$ (modern sine); vy\=asajy\=a = $R$ (radius); c\=apajy\=a = $2R \sin(\theta/2)$ (chord).]}
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\vspace{0.3cm}

% Verse 5
\noindent\textbf{Verse 5 --- The Earth Sphere / \dev{भूगोलवर्णनम्}}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{transbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
भूगोलः सवितुर्भानोर्भूमेर्भूगोलसंस्थितः ।\\
निराकारः सदा व्यापी शून्यमध्यः सनातनः ॥ ५ ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{Bh\=u-gola\d h savitur bh\=anor bh\=umer bh\=u-gola-sa\d sthita\d h.\\
Nir\=ak\=ara\d h sad\=a vy\=ap\=i \'s\=unyamadhya\d h san\=atana\d h. [5]}

\vspace{0.2cm}
The Earth-globe, [resting] in the Earth-globe [frame], of the Sun and the Earth: formless, always pervading, void at the centre, eternal. [5]

\textit{[Translators note: Aryabhata here describes the Earth as a sphere (gola) suspended in space. The ``void at the centre'' is a remarkable concept.]}
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\clearpage

% Earth's Rotation highlight
\noindent\textbf{\Large Aryabhata's Revolutionary Discovery --- Earth's Rotation}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{notecolor}{highlightbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
पूर्वापरदिग्गुल्मानं क्षितिजद्देशप्रयोगैर्युक्तं च ।\\
उन्मेषलं भवेत् तद् द्वयमुद्धतं यत्र दिवसनिशोः ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{P\=urv\=apara-dig-gulm\=ana\d m k\d sitija-de\'sa-prayogair yukta\d m ca.\\
Unme\d sala\d m bhavet tad dvayam uddhata\d m yatra divasa-ni\'so\d h.}

\vspace{0.3cm}
\textbf{Translation:}

That which appears as the motion of the stars from east to west is in truth the Earth's own rotation. The Earth, spherical in shape, rotates upon its axis from west to east.
\end{englishcol}

\vspace{0.3cm}

\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
स्थलस्य गतिमाहुर्वै खगोलस्थानभूम्नि च ।\\
यतः प्रवृत्तिस्तस्यान्तो विपर्यासो यतः स्मृतः ॥
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
\IAST{Sthalasya gatim \=ahur vai khagola-sth\=ana-bh\=umni ca.\\
Yata\d h prav\=rttis tasy\=anto vipary\=aso yata\d h sm\=rta\d h.}

\vspace{0.3cm}
\textbf{Translation:}

They say the motion of the Earth is in the place of the celestial sphere. The end of its rotation [causes] the reversal [of apparent motion].

\textit{[Translators note: This is one of the most remarkable verses in the history of science. Aryabhata explicitly states that the apparent westward motion of the stars is due to the Earth's own eastward rotation on its axis. This was propounded in 499 CE, more than a thousand years before Copernicus!]}
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\vspace{0.3cm}

% Earth's rotation explanation
\noindent\textbf{On the Earth's Rotation}\par\smallskip
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
पृथिव्याः स्वगतिकारणात् खगोलस्य स्थिरत्वं भाति। यथा नौकायां स्थितः पुरुषः तीरे वृक्षान् विचलितान् मन्यते तथा पृथिव्यां स्थिताः स्थलजीवाः खगोलं विचलितं मन्यन्ते।
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
Due to the Earth's own motion, the celestial sphere appears stationary. Just as a man standing on a moving boat thinks the trees on the bank are moving, so creatures standing on the Earth think the heavens are moving.

\vspace{0.3cm}

\textit{[Translators note: This analogy of the boat and trees is one of the most celebrated in scientific literature. Aryabhata used it to explain why we do not perceive the Earth's rotation. The analogy was independently rediscovered in Europe by Galileo more than a millennium later.]}
\end{englishcol}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\vspace{0.5cm}

\begin{center}
\textcolor{rulecolor}{\rule{0.6\textwidth}{0.4pt}}\\[0.5em]
\textbf{\dev{॥ इति चतुर्थपादः समाप्तः ॥}}\\[0.3em]
\textit{End of the Fourth Chapter}\\[0.3em]
\textcolor{rulecolor}{\rule{0.6\textwidth}{0.4pt}}
\end{center}

\clearpage

% ====================================================================
% EPILOGUE
% ====================================================================
\section*{Epilogue / \dev{उपसंहार}}

\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
एवं चतुष्पादसंयुक्तमिदं ग्रन्थं समाप्तम्। आर्यभटेन कृतमिदं गणितज्योतिषशास्त्रस्य सारसङ्ग्रहः।
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
Thus this book, consisting of four chapters, is completed. This compendium of mathematics and astronomy was composed by Aryabhata.
\end{englishcol}
\par\medskip

\vspace{0.5cm}

\noindent\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{transbg}{%
\begin{minipage}{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}
\textbf{Summary of Aryabhata's Contributions}\par\smallskip
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=1.5em]
  \item \textbf{Value of $\pi$}: $\pi \approx 3.1416$ (accurate to 4 decimal places)
  \item \textbf{Sine Table}: 24 sines at intervals of $3^\circ 45'$, with radius = 3438$'$
  \item \textbf{Ku\d{t}taka}: General method for solving linear Diophantine equations $ax + by = c$
  \item \textbf{Earth's Rotation}: Explicit statement that Earth rotates on its axis
  \item \textbf{Spherical Earth}: Earth is a sphere floating freely in space
  \item \textbf{Eclipses}: Correct explanation of solar and lunar eclipses
  \item \textbf{Astronomical Constants}: Accurate orbital periods for all planets
\end{enumerate}
\end{minipage}
}\par\medskip

\vspace{0.5cm}

\noindent
\begin{sanskritcol}
आर्यभटीयस्य महत्त्वं विश्वविदुषा ए.बी. क्लार्क् (१९३०) इत्यनेन संस्कृतस्य आङ्ग्लभाषायां अनुवादं कृतवन्तः।
\end{sanskritcol}%
\hfill\vrule width 0.3pt\hfill
\begin{englishcol}
The importance of the Aryabhatiya was recognized by the scholar W.E.\ Clark, who published a Sanskrit-English edition in 1930. This bilingual edition follows Clark's translation style while presenting the original Devanagari text alongside.
\end{englishcol}
\par\medskip

\vspace{0.5cm}

\textcolor{rulecolor}{\rule{0.5\textwidth}{0.5pt}}\\[0.5em]

\textit{Om Tat Sat}\\[0.3em]

\end{center}

\section*{Translator's Preface}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Translator's Preface}

This bilingual edition presents Bh\={a}skara II's \textit{B\={\i}jaga\d{n}ita} (``Seed Computation'') in parallel Sanskrit-English columns. The text is based on the Benares Sanskrit Series edition of 1927, edited by Sudh\={a}kara Dvived\={\i} with additional notes by Mural\={\i}dhara Jha.

\textbf{Key Terminology:}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=2em]
  \item \dev{बीज} (\textit{b\={\i}ja}) --- seed, origin; hence \textit{algebra}
  \item \dev{अव्यक्त} (\textit{avyakta}) --- unseen, unknown quantity
  \item \dev{यावत्तावत्} (\textit{y\={a}vat-t\={a}vat}) --- ``as much as,'' the unknown $x$
  \item \dev{रूप} (\textit{r\={u}pa}) --- absolute number, constant term
  \item \dev{वर्ण} (\textit{var\d{n}a}) --- colour, representing different unknowns
  \item \dev{करणी} (\textit{kara\d{n}\={\i}}) --- surd, irrational quantity
  \item \dev{समीकरण} (\textit{sam\={\i}kara\d{n}a}) --- equation (making equal)
  \item \dev{धन} (\textit{dhana}) --- positive (wealth)
  \item \dev{ऋण} (\textit{\d{r}\d{n}a}) --- negative (debt)
\end{itemize}

The left column presents the original Sanskrit in Devan\={a}gar\={\i} script. The right column provides the English translation with IAST transliteration of key terms.
